tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about using a group chat for class. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is one short class summary with dates and places. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a class chat works well with clear topics and short messages. A quick message reaches classmates in different places and tells us about a changed room or meeting time. Also, one notice keeps dates and tasks together and helps me plan several school days with my notebook open. For example, yesterday our group put the room change in one short message. We kept casual conversation separate, so every student found the new room number quickly. This gives us something real to talk about at the meeting.

I will collect the class dates from the official course notice. Could you please check the room numbers against our timetable? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notes, and we can keep one copy of the plan for both of us.

Let me know if another time is better for you.

Thanks,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about asking a teacher questions. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「向老師提問」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about asking a teacher questions. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is two clear questions for our teacher before practice. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think immediate safety questions and planned vocabulary questions both matter. A question shows the teacher the part that confuses me, so the explanation can focus on my real difficulty. But a busy teacher also helps other students, and a suitable time gives us space for a useful conversation. For example, yesterday I stopped a simulation exercise and asked my teacher about an unclear safety step. Later I wrote a separate vocabulary question in my notebook for our discussion. We can start from this small example when we meet.

I will write one question about the simulation instructions. Could you please bring the page that explains the same classroom task? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring a printed copy of our notes and share the final version afterwards.

Please message me if you need to change the plan.

See you then,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about learning nursing words in context. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「把護理單字放進情境學」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about learning nursing words in context. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is five vocabulary cards with matching example sentences. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a few basic words plus simple examples help me understand a new topic. A sentence shows the job of a word, so I see more than a translation beside the English spelling. Also, I can check basic meanings quickly on one page before reading the longer explanations in my nursing textbook. For example, yesterday I checked five new words on a small list. After that I read one simple example for each word and said the examples aloud. I think this example will make our discussion easier.

I will choose five new words from the current nursing lesson. Could you please find a simple textbook example for each selected word? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will take photos of our final notes and send them to you after the meeting.

If something comes up, just send me a message.

Talk soon,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about simulation practice with a partner. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「和同學做模擬練習」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about simulation practice with a partner. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a short list of teacher feedback from the simulation. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a teacher demonstration and partner practice support different parts of learning. A partner listens to my explanation and tells me about unclear words, so I can practise a complete introduction. Also, the teacher explains the purpose of each step and answers our questions before we practise together in the classroom. For example, yesterday I watched the teacher's introduction first. Then I practised a short introduction with a classmate and asked the teacher about one unclear phrase. It is a good place to begin our planning together.

I will prepare a simple student introduction from our lesson. Could you please play the fictional patient role during teacher-supervised practice? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook so that we can write the final plan together.

Tell me soon if this time does not work for you.

Cheers,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about writing a learning reflection. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「寫學習反思」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about writing a learning reflection. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is two short reflections without real patient details. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think brief notes after class and a reflection later fit my study routine. I choose one learning point from the day, so my review has a clear focus instead of a long list. Also, brief notes protect the order of events in my memory and give me material for a longer review later. For example, yesterday I wrote three short facts after class without patient details. After dinner I added my feelings and one simple goal for the next lesson. This experience gives us a useful starting point for a short discussion.

I will choose one classroom learning event from last week. Could you please bring a blank reflection sheet with space for one next step? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook and keep a copy of our final work for the next review.

Please tell me about any changes to the time.

See you,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about taking notes during orientation. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「在實習說明時做筆記」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about taking notes during orientation. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a student checklist with verified times and contacts. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think the official handout with a few personal questions is useful for orientation. I can record a meeting place or contact number quickly and find it again before the next group activity. But I sometimes miss a point during fast writing, and careful listening is important during the first explanation to our group. For example, yesterday I followed the orientation handout with my classmates. I wrote one personal question beside a heading and checked the answer with our teacher. This gives us something real to talk about at the meeting.

I will check our copy of the orientation handout. Could you please list the meeting places from the course notice? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notes, and we can keep one copy of the plan for both of us.

Let me know if another time is better for you.

Thanks,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about learning an introduction for practice. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「練習實習時的自我介紹」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about learning an introduction for practice. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is two clear introduction sentences for supervised role play. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a few key sentences make a simple introduction clear. My name and student role tell the other person about me, so the start of our classroom conversation is clear. Also, simple words leave space for the other person to speak and make the exchange easy to follow in class. For example, yesterday I practised my name and student role before simulation class. During the exercise I used those two sentences and listened to my classmate's reply. We can start from this small example when we meet.

I will write a short introduction with my name and student role. Could you please listen for unclear words during our practice? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring a printed copy of our notes and share the final version afterwards.

Please message me if you need to change the plan.

See you then,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about asking for feedback after practice. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「練習後請老師回饋」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about asking for feedback after practice. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is one revised example for our teacher to check. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a brief overall review helps me choose one useful next step. One specific correction gives me a small task, so I know exactly what to practise after the lesson. Also, a quick review also identifies a successful point and helps me keep that part during my next supervised attempt. For example, yesterday my teacher named one strength and one difficulty after our exercise. I kept the clear opening and practised the difficult question before the next round. I think this example will make our discussion easier.

I will bring the written feedback from our last classroom exercise. Could you please help me identify the one point that needs another attempt? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will take photos of our final notes and send them to you after the meeting.

If something comes up, just send me a message.

Talk soon,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about reviewing English during a bus trip. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「利用搭公車的時間複習英文」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about reviewing English during a bus trip. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is two small task lists for different study conditions. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think my bus routine needs room for both a small review and a rest. A few familiar words fit a short journey, so I do not need a long desk session for every review. But a crowded journey is not a comfortable place for careful reading, so I keep the difficult task for my desk. For example, yesterday the morning bus was quiet, so I reviewed three words in my seat. After class the bus was crowded, so I took a break. It is a good place to begin our planning together.

I will choose five familiar words for a short bus review. Could you please prepare a separate desk task for difficult reading? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook so that we can write the final plan together.

Tell me soon if this time does not work for you.

Cheers,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about preparing a bag the night before. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「前一天晚上準備書包」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about preparing a bag the night before. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a bag checklist with space for one last morning check. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think an evening bag check and a morning update fit my school routine. My books are ready beside the door, so I do not search for different notebooks during breakfast before school. But I still use some books at night, and a morning check keeps the last study items in the correct bag. For example, yesterday I packed my usual books after dinner. This morning I checked the class message and added the extra handout for our first lesson. This experience gives us a useful starting point for a short discussion.

I will list the books and materials for our next lesson. Could you please check the list against the newest class notice? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook and keep a copy of our final work for the next review.

Please tell me about any changes to the time.

See you,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about setting one small English goal. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「為英文設定一個小目標」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about setting one small English goal. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a small learning goal with a clear example of success. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a short look at the lesson helps me choose a useful goal. A clear goal tells me what to practise, so I spend the session on one sentence pattern or a few words. But a new example sometimes reveals a gap in my knowledge and changes the point that needs practice after class. For example, yesterday I read the lesson once before setting my goal. I noticed a question pattern and chose that pattern for ten minutes of focused practice. This gives us something real to talk about at the meeting.

I will bring three sentences from my most recent practice. Could you please choose one pattern for a short focused exercise? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notes, and we can keep one copy of the plan for both of us.

Let me know if another time is better for you.

Thanks,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about keeping old English answers. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「保留以前寫過的英文答案」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about keeping old English answers. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a review folder arranged by sentence pattern. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a small organised review collection helps me find useful examples. An earlier answer shows a specific mistake, so I can compare it with my current sentence during review. Also, a small organised collection is easy to review and leaves space for the newest questions from my current lessons. For example, yesterday I chose one early answer and its corrected version for my review folder. I kept the other notes in order for later reference. We can start from this small example when we meet.

I will bring an early answer and its corrected version. Could you please choose another answer that shows a different pattern? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring a printed copy of our notes and share the final version afterwards.

Please message me if you need to change the plan.

See you then,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about practising for a future nursing job in the US. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「為未來赴美從事護理練英文」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about practising for a future nursing job in the US. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a weekly English plan connected with the nursing goal. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a long-term goal and a small weekly task belong in the same plan. The goal connects English with work that matters to me, so even a short introduction has a clear use. Also, a weekly task is close to my present level and shows exactly what I need to practise after school. For example, yesterday I wrote my long-term nursing goal at the top of my notebook. Below it I added one small task with three present-tense sentences. I think this example will make our discussion easier.

I will write one long-term goal in plain words. Could you please help me turn that goal into one small weekly task? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will take photos of our final notes and send them to you after the meeting.

If something comes up, just send me a message.

Talk soon,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about sharing an English practice plan with family. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「和家人分享英文練習計畫」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about sharing an English practice plan with family. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a clear two-sentence update about this week's learning. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a clear main goal and flexible daily details work well for my family. My family knows the time for my practice, so we can arrange a short quiet period around dinner at home. But I need space to notice my own difficulties and adjust the practice to the lesson in front of me. For example, yesterday I told my family about my main goal for the week. I chose the exact evening exercise later after checking my homework and energy. It is a good place to begin our planning together.

I will prepare a short explanation of my current English task. Could you please listen to the explanation and note any unclear part? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook so that we can write the final plan together.

Tell me soon if this time does not work for you.

Cheers,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about using a dictionary during writing. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「寫作時使用字典」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about using a dictionary during writing. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a checked draft with three useful vocabulary notes. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a simple first draft and a few dictionary checks suit my writing practice. A clear example shows the word in a sentence, so I can check its meaning and place in my own answer. But familiar words match my current level and help me practise a complete idea without a long search for difficult expressions. For example, yesterday I drafted three sentences with words from my lesson. I checked one uncertain spelling in the dictionary and read the complete answer aloud. This experience gives us a useful starting point for a short discussion.

I will bring three words from my recent writing attempt. Could you please find a learner-dictionary example for each word? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook and keep a copy of our final work for the next review.

Please tell me about any changes to the time.

See you,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about reading the task before writing. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「先讀懂題目再開始寫」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about reading the task before writing. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is two brief writing plans that answer the whole task. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a full task check with a small writing plan helps me answer clearly. The task names the topic and the number of sentences, so I know the size and purpose of my answer. Also, a simple list of required points gives me a clear guide and helps me return to the task during writing. For example, yesterday I read the whole task and marked its action words. I wrote a tiny plan beside it and checked the requirements after my first draft. This gives us something real to talk about at the meeting.

I will bring two short writing prompts from our lesson. Could you please mark the number of sentences and the required grammar? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notes, and we can keep one copy of the plan for both of us.

Let me know if another time is better for you.

Thanks,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about reading a draft aloud. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「把自己寫的草稿念出來」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about reading a draft aloud. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is one revised draft with clear subjects and verbs. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think a silent meaning check and spoken practice both help me improve a draft. A complete spoken sentence makes a missing subject or verb noticeable, so I stop and check that part of the draft. But a silent check also respects other students in the library and gives me a quiet way to review the whole paragraph. For example, yesterday I first compared my paragraph with the task in silence. After dinner I read it aloud in my room and checked one repeated word. We can start from this small example when we meet.

I will bring a short draft with three complete sentences. Could you please listen to the draft after our silent task check? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring a printed copy of our notes and share the final version afterwards.

Please message me if you need to change the plan.

See you then,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about learning from a corrected answer. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「從批改後的答案學習」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about learning from a corrected answer. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a new sentence with the same corrected pattern. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think one independent correction and a teacher example both help me learn. The correction shows a clear version of my own idea, so I can connect the explanation with my original sentence. Also, one independent correction gives me a chance to use the lesson and shows the exact point that still needs help. For example, yesterday I tried to correct one verb before opening the full example. I compared the two versions and wrote a new sentence with the corrected pattern. I think this example will make our discussion easier.

I will bring one original answer and the teacher's feedback. Could you please hide the full answer during my first correction attempt? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will take photos of our final notes and send them to you after the meeting.

If something comes up, just send me a message.

Talk soon,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about taking a short break between study tasks. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「在兩項讀書任務中間休息」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about taking a short break between study tasks. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a study plan with a short break after each completed section. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think planning breaks around clear stopping points helps me study. A break gives me a chance to leave the desk briefly and return to the next task with a clear beginning. Also, a finished task gives me a clear stopping point and lets me begin the next section without an unfinished sentence nearby. For example, yesterday I planned a break after one small English exercise. The task ended at a clear point, so I returned from the break to a new page. It is a good place to begin our planning together.

I will list the short tasks for one afternoon at the library. Could you please suggest clear stopping points between the tasks? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook so that we can write the final plan together.

Tell me soon if this time does not work for you.

Cheers,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about checking classmates' practice answers. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「互看同學的練習答案」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about checking classmates' practice answers. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a peer review sheet with a separate teacher question. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think classmates can check simple points and bring uncertain questions to the teacher. Another student reads my words without knowing my first idea, so unclear parts become easy to identify during our discussion. Also, the teacher explains the rule clearly and connects the correction with the pattern in our current lesson on the board. For example, yesterday my partner checked my subjects and full stops. We found one uncertain verb and asked our teacher to explain that point before changing the answer. This experience gives us a useful starting point for a short discussion.

I will prepare a simple checklist for subjects and full stops. Could you please bring one practice answer with an uncertain grammar point? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notebook and keep a copy of our final work for the next review.

Please tell me about any changes to the time.

See you,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write an email to a classmate planning a short meeting about keeping practice patient stories fictional. Explain the purpose, suggest work for each person, give a clear time and place, and say what you want to finish.
tasks.zh: 寫信和同學約一次「使用虛構病人情境練英文」的小練習。分段寫目的、兩人各自準備什麼、時間地點，以及結束時要完成的成果；至少 120 字。用 will 說安排，用 Could you please 提出禮貌請求。
tasks.sample:
Hi Amy,

I am writing about keeping practice patient stories fictional. I want to meet in the school discussion room at four on Wednesday. Our aim is a short classroom dialogue without real patient information. Could you please tell me whether that time works for you?

I think daily examples can lead to a useful fictional nursing exercise. A fictional case gives the class a shared situation for role play without using a real person's private details. Also, daily situations use words from my earlier lessons, so I can focus on the subject and verb in the sentence. For example, yesterday I first asked a classmate simple questions about school. Later we used the same question pattern in a fictional nursing exercise under our teacher's guidance. This gives us something real to talk about at the meeting.

I will bring three simple questions about school life. Could you please help me adapt one question to a fictional supervised role play? We will compare our ideas with the course notes and write down any questions for our teacher. I will bring my notes, and we can keep one copy of the plan for both of us.

Let me know if another time is better for you.

Thanks,
Xuanye

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about using a short daily study list. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「每天列一張短讀書清單」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about using a short daily study list in my school life. My view is that a study list is useful with room for small changes. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, a short list gives me a clear first task, so I do not spend my whole break choosing work. Also, I can mark each finished task on the paper, and this shows my progress during a busy day. For example, yesterday I put three English tasks on my list. I finished the first two before dinner and checked the last one after dinner. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But a long class sometimes changes my free time, so a fixed plan does not fit the whole afternoon. Some questions need extra practice, and I want to give these difficult points enough attention at my desk. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

In conclusion, I still believe a study list is useful with room for small changes. For my next step, I will bring a list of my unfinished assignments. I will discuss the result with a classmate and keep the useful points in my study notes.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about studying in the school library. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「在學校圖書館讀書」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about studying in the school library in my school life. My view is that I need different study places for different kinds of homework. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, the quiet tables help me read one page at a time without music from the next room. Also, I can use the nursing books on the shelves and check unfamiliar words in the same place. For example, last Monday I reviewed a nursing chapter near the library window. I found a useful picture in another book and understood the lesson. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But some books stay in my dormitory, so I sometimes need to carry a heavy bag to the library. I can practise English aloud in my room, but the quiet library area is not suitable for this activity. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

To sum up, I need different study places for different kinds of homework. For my next step, I will check the library opening times before our meeting. After one week, I will check whether this plan really helps me.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about studying with a partner. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「和一位同學一起讀書」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about studying with a partner in my school life. My view is that partner practice is useful after a short period of individual study. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, a partner explains an idea in different words, and this sometimes makes the meaning clear to me. Also, we can ask each other questions, so we notice gaps in our knowledge before the next class. For example, last week my classmate asked me five questions about body parts. I missed two answers, so we checked the textbook together after class. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But I read slowly at first, and I need time for the words that are new to me. A partner sometimes starts another topic, so I lose my place in the paragraph during our conversation. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

Overall, I still believe partner practice is useful after a short period of individual study. For my next step, I will prepare five questions from our current chapter. If it works, I will keep it as part of my weekly routine.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about managing phone notifications during study. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「讀書時的手機通知」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about managing phone notifications during study in my school life. My view is that I can limit ordinary notifications and keep important class messages. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, each message takes my attention away from the page, so I need time to find my place again. Also, a quiet phone gives me one clear task at a time and helps me finish a small reading exercise. For example, yesterday I silenced my phone for twenty minutes at my desk. I finished one English page and checked my messages during my break. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But our teacher sometimes changes a meeting place, and I need that message before my group leaves the dormitory. My family also needs a way to reach me about important arrangements during a long day away from home. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

All in all, I still believe I can limit ordinary notifications and keep important class messages. For my next step, I will write down the types of messages from our class. I will also ask my teacher for one piece of advice about it.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about using a paper notebook for English. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「用紙本筆記本學英文」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about using a paper notebook for English in my school life. My view is that paper notes and digital notes have different jobs in my review. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, I can write a new word beside a simple picture, and this makes the page personal to me. Also, the notebook opens quickly on my desk, so I can review a few words without checking other apps. For example, last Friday I drew a hand beside the word hand in my notebook. I covered the word and remembered it during my evening review. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But I do not carry my paper notebook on every trip, so I sometimes have no notes during a wait for the bus. I can search for an old word quickly and keep related examples together without another heavy book. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

In short, I still believe paper notes and digital notes have different jobs in my review. For my next step, I will bring one page of paper notes and one digital example. Then I will write a short note about what worked and what did not.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about doing a short evening review. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「每天晚上做短時間複習」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about doing a short evening review in my school life. My view is that a flexible review time helps me keep a regular study habit. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, the lesson is still clear in my memory after class, so I can connect my notes with the teacher's explanation. Also, a small review task fits before dinner and gives me a clear place to start the next lesson. For example, yesterday I read five English sentences before dinner in my dormitory. I corrected one verb in my notebook and asked about it the next day. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But I often feel tired after a long school day, so careful reading takes a lot of effort at night. The early morning is quiet in my room, and I can study a few notes before the first class. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

To conclude, I still believe a flexible review time helps me keep a regular study habit. For my next step, I will list the free periods around our nursing classes. I will discuss the result with a classmate and keep the useful points in my study notes.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about speaking English aloud. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「把英文句子念出來」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about speaking English aloud in my school life. My view is that I need both silent reading and spoken practice in my English study. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, I notice missing words more easily in a spoken sentence, so I check the sentence again in my notebook. Also, my voice gives me practice with a full sentence instead of only separate words from a vocabulary list. For example, last Thursday I read my introduction aloud to a classmate. I forgot the word am at first, so I practised the complete sentence again. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But a new text contains several unfamiliar words, and I need time to understand their meaning before speaking. I share a small room with another student, so quiet study respects my roommate's rest during the evening. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

In conclusion, I need both silent reading and spoken practice in my English study. For my next step, I will choose a short dialogue from our textbook. After one week, I will check whether this plan really helps me.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about using colour in class notes. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「在筆記中使用顏色」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about using colour in class notes in my school life. My view is that a few colours for key points are enough for my class notes. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, one colour marks the main idea, so I can find the start of a topic quickly before a test. Also, a second colour marks my questions and reminds me about the parts that need another explanation from the teacher. For example, last week I marked three questions in blue on my nursing notes. tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「先讀懂題目再開始寫」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about reading the task before writing in my school life. My view is that a full task check with a small writing plan helps me answer clearly. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, the task names the topic and the number of sentences, so I know the size and purpose of my answer. Also, I find the required grammar and keep that pattern in mind instead of writing unrelated details about another topic. For example, yesterday I marked the words three sentences in my English task. I wrote exactly three complete sentences and checked the required verbs beside the prompt. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But a long prompt sometimes feels difficult at first, and repeated reading without a small plan does not solve every unclear part. A simple list of required points gives me a clear guide and helps me return to the task during writing. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

Overall, I still believe a full task check with a small writing plan helps me answer clearly. For my next step, I will bring two short writing prompts from our lesson. After one week, I will check whether this plan really helps me.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about reading a draft aloud. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「把自己寫的草稿念出來」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about reading a draft aloud in my school life. My view is that a silent meaning check and spoken practice both help me improve a draft. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, a complete spoken sentence makes a missing subject or verb noticeable, so I stop and check that part of the draft. Also, I hear repeated words in nearby sentences and choose a clear revision from the language in my current lesson. For example, yesterday I read my short introduction aloud at my desk. One sentence sounded incomplete, so I found its missing verb and corrected the sentence. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But a smooth sentence sometimes expresses the wrong idea, so I first compare the meaning with the writing task. A silent check also respects other students in the library and gives me a quiet way to review the whole paragraph. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

All in all, I still believe a silent meaning check and spoken practice both help me improve a draft. For my next step, I will bring a short draft with three complete sentences. If it works, I will keep it as part of my weekly routine.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about learning from a corrected answer. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「從批改後的答案學習」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about learning from a corrected answer in my school life. My view is that one independent correction and a teacher example both help me learn. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, the correction shows a clear version of my own idea, so I can connect the explanation with my original sentence. Also, I can identify one important pattern and practise it in a new situation instead of copying the whole answer without thought. For example, yesterday my teacher corrected one question in my draft. I compared the word order and wrote another question about school with the same pattern. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But an immediate full answer makes copying easy, and I sometimes miss the reason for the change during a quick review. One independent correction gives me a chance to use the lesson and shows the exact point that still needs help. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

In short, I still believe one independent correction and a teacher example both help me learn. For my next step, I will bring one original answer and the teacher's feedback. I will also ask my teacher for one piece of advice about it.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about taking a short break between study tasks. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.
tasks.zh: 給同學看的一篇短文：談「在兩項讀書任務中間休息」。分段寫立場、理由與具體經驗，再交代一個限制和接下來的做法；至少 120 字。每段各做一件事，不把整篇擠成一段。
tasks.sample:
I often think about taking a short break between study tasks in my school life. My view is that planning breaks around clear stopping points helps me study. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, a break gives me a chance to leave the desk briefly and return to the next task with a clear beginning. Also, I can check my next goal during the pause and avoid moving straight into a long unplanned session on my phone. For example, yesterday I closed my book after twenty minutes and stood up for a short break. Then I returned to the desk and started the next exercise. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But a break in the middle of one short question breaks the flow, and I need time to remember my place again. A finished task gives me a clear stopping point and lets me begin the next section without an unfinished sentence nearby. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

To conclude, I still believe planning breaks around clear stopping points helps me study. For my next step, I will list the short tasks for one afternoon at the library. Then I will write a short note about what worked and what did not.

tasks.prompt: Write a short piece for your class about checking classmates' practice answers. Explain your position, develop your reasons with one experience, mention a limitation, and finish with your next practical step. Use separate paragraphs.

tasks.sample:
I often think about checking classmates' practice answers in my school life. My view is that classmates can check simple points and bring uncertain questions to the teacher. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, another student reads my words without knowing my first idea, so unclear parts become easy to identify during our discussion. Also, I learn from checking a classmate's answer and compare both examples with the current lesson in our textbook. For example, yesterday my classmate read my three English sentences and found a missing subject. I checked the textbook and revised the sentence before showing it to our teacher. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But a new grammar point confuses both students sometimes, and two similar guesses do not make an answer correct in class. The teacher explains the rule clearly and connects the correction with the pattern in our current lesson on the board. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

In conclusion, I still believe classmates can check simple points and bring uncertain questions to the teacher. For my next step, I will prepare a simple checklist for subjects and full stops. I will discuss the result with a classmate and keep the useful points in my study notes.

I often think about keeping practice patient stories fictional in my school life. My view is that daily examples can lead to a useful fictional nursing exercise. I want a method that fits an ordinary week of nursing classes and English practice.

First, a fictional case gives the class a shared situation for role play without using a real person's private details. Also, I can connect a familiar sentence pattern with a nursing setting and ask the teacher about suitable words during practice. For example, yesterday our teacher gave us a fictional patient name for an introduction exercise. I practised the conversation with a classmate and kept real patient information out. This experience shows one useful part of the method in my own daily routine.

But a new language pattern already needs attention, and unfamiliar clinical words add another difficult part to the first attempt. Daily situations use words from my earlier lessons, so I can focus on the subject and verb in the sentence. These limits matter during a busy day, so I do not use exactly the same plan for every situation.

To sum up, I still believe daily examples can lead to a useful fictional nursing exercise. For my next step, I will bring three simple questions about school life. After one week, I will check whether this plan really helps me.

tasks.prompt: Write an email to the organiser of a school English club. Introduce yourself as a nursing student, explain your current level and goal, ask about beginner activities, and request the next meeting details.
tasks.zh: 寫信給學校英文社的負責人：介紹自己是護理系學生，交代目前程度與目標，詢問初學者活動和下次聚會資訊。用稱呼、三段內容與結尾；至少 120 字。
tasks.sample:
Dear English Club Team,

My name is Xuanye, and I am a nursing student in Taiwan. I am writing to ask about your club. My English is still basic, but I practise a few simple sentences every day. My long-term goal is to work as a nurse in the United States.

I want to join an activity that gives beginners time to think and speak. At present I can introduce myself and ask a few questions about school. I am still learning to give reasons and write clear paragraphs. Could you please tell me which activities are suitable for students at this level?

I also want to know the date, time, and place of your next meeting. I will bring my notebook and prepare a short introduction. Thank you for your help.

Yours sincerely,
Xuanye

grammar.title: 把文章分段：開頭交代目的，內容展開，結尾收好
points: 第一段交代寫作目的；信件先有稱呼，結尾加感謝與署名，語氣跟對象相配。
中間一段負責一個重點；敘事照時間寫，說意見則把理由和例子放在一起。
說進行中的事用 be＋動詞 -ing（am feeling／was shaking）；說接下來的安排可用 will＋原形動詞。
禮貌請求可用 Could you please…；tell me 後面若再接問題，改用主詞在動詞前的順序。

examples.en: I am writing to ask about yesterday's class.
examples.zh: 我寫信是想詢問昨天的課。（開頭說明目的。）

examples.en: I missed class because I was sick.
examples.zh: 我因為生病而缺課。（接著說明事情。）

examples.en: Could you please tell me which pages I should read?
examples.zh: 請問您可以告訴我該讀哪些頁嗎？（which pages 後面是 I should read，不倒裝。）

examples.en: I will come to class tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我明天會來上課。（will 後面用原形 come。）

examples.en: Thank you for your help.
examples.zh: 謝謝您的協助。（用合適的句子收尾。）

mistakes.bad: Could you tell me what should I study?
mistakes.good: Could you tell me what I should study?
mistakes.why: 問題放進 tell me 後面時，順序改成 I should study。
will 後面直接用原形動詞，不加 to。

stages.name: ⑩ 描述數字和變化（Task 1 暖身）
stages.goal: 先用簡單句讀懂小圖表，寫出上升、下降、不變與最高最低。
criteria: 開頭說圖表在記什麼，並用一句話說主要變化
挑出數字，至少寫一次變化或比較
from…to… 寫起點和終點，by… 寫增加或減少多少
數字與單位符合圖表，不猜原因，整題至少 80 字

grammar.title: 看圖說數字：rise／fall、from…to…、by…
points: 先用 The chart shows… 說圖表內容，再用 Overall 說最明顯的整體變化；只描述圖上有的資訊。
上升是 rise，下降是 fall，不變是 stay the same；說已過去的資料時用 rose、fell、stayed the same。
from 10 to 20 表示從 10 到 20；rose by 10 表示增加 10。by 後面是差額，不是最後的數字。
the highest／the lowest 表示最高／最低；兩個數字相同可以寫 had the same number，別忘記分鐘、人次等單位。

examples.en: The chart shows daily clinic visits.
examples.zh: 圖表呈現診所每天的看診人次。

examples.en: The number rose from 20 to 30.
examples.zh: 數字從 20 增加到 30。

examples.en: The number fell by 10.
examples.zh: 數字減少了 10。

examples.en: The figure stayed the same on Thursday.
examples.zh: 週四的數字維持不變。

examples.en: Tuesday had the highest figure, and Friday had the lowest.
examples.zh: 週二的數字最高，週五最低。

mistakes.bad: The number rose from 20 to 30, an increase of 30.
mistakes.good: The number rose from 20 to 30, an increase of 10.
mistakes.why: 30 是終點；增加量要算 30 減 20，所以是 10。

mistakes.bad: Tuesday had the most highest figure.
mistakes.why: highest 已經是最高，不要再加 most。

stages.name: ⑪ 雅思 Task 1
stages.goal: 描述圖表：總覽＋重點數據＋比較
criteria: Task Achievement：有總覽（overview），挑出重要數據並比較
Coherence & Cohesion：段落清楚、用對連接詞
Lexical Resource：描述趨勢的用字多樣（rise、drop、remain stable）
Grammatical Range & Accuracy：句型有變化、錯誤少

tasks.prompt: The chart shows a patient's systolic blood pressure from Monday to Friday. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 圖表是一位病人週一到週五的收縮壓。挑出重點描述並比較。

chart.title: Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)

tasks.sample:
The line graph shows changes in one patient's systolic blood pressure over five days, from Monday to Friday.

Overall, the patient's blood pressure declined over the week, apart from one day when it remained stable. By the end of the period, it was much lower than at the start.

On Monday, the reading was at its highest point of the week, 150 mmHg. It then dropped by 8 mmHg to 142 mmHg on Tuesday and fell more sharply to 130 mmHg on Wednesday. This was the biggest daily decrease, 12 mmHg.

On Thursday, the figure stayed the same at 130 mmHg. By Friday, the blood pressure had decreased again to 124 mmHg, which was the lowest reading in the period. In total, it went down by 26 mmHg between Monday and Friday, so Friday's reading was about one sixth lower than Monday's.

In short, most of the fall happened in the first half of the week: the reading dropped by 20 mmHg from Monday to Wednesday, but by only 6 mmHg from Wednesday to Friday.

tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料：參加社區無障礙調查的人數，比較同一個月六個中心的數字。寫至少 150 字：改寫圖表資訊、用一段說整體重點，再用數字支持比較。不要猜原因或把練習數字當成真實統計。
tasks.sample:
The chart presents the number of participants in a community accessibility survey at six fictional centres in the same study month. It allows a comparison of the reported counts, with each figure expressed in participants.

Overall, the largest figure belonged to Centre F, whereas Centre A had the smallest. These are comparisons between centres, rather than changes over time.

Looking first at Centres A, B and C, the figures were 97, 109 and 205 participants, respectively. Together, these three centres accounted for 411 participants. Centre B recorded 12 more participants than Centre A.

The remaining centres, D, E and F, recorded 209, 217 and 225 participants, respectively. Their combined figure was 651 participants, compared with 411 for the first group. Across all six centres, the total was 1062 participants. The last three centres therefore accounted for about 61 percent of the sum, with the other centres accounting for the remainder. The difference between the highest and lowest figures was 128 participants.

chart.title: Participants in a community accessibility survey (participants; fictional data)

tasks.prompt: The chart shows the number of students completing a library research lesson from January to June in a fictional study year. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料：完成圖書館資料搜尋課的學生數，比較一到六月的變化。寫至少 150 字：改寫圖表資訊、用一段說整體重點，再用數字支持比較。不要猜原因或把練習數字當成真實統計。
tasks.sample:
The chart presents the number of students completing a library research lesson from January to June in a fictional study year. It allows a comparison of the reported counts, with each figure expressed in students.

Overall, the final figure was higher than the initial one. The figure rose overall despite several reversals. The highest value occurred in June, while January recorded the lowest.

In January, the figure stood at 55 students. It then rose by 14 students, from 55 to 69 in February. Moving from February to March, it fell by 8 students, from 69 to 61. Comparing the first and third months directly, the difference was 6 students.

The second half of the chart began with 73 students in April. The figure then fell by 8 students, from 73 to 65 in May and rose by 15 students, from 65 to 80 in June. The average monthly count was about 61.7 students in the first half of the period, compared with about 72.7 in the second half. The difference between the highest and lowest figures was 25 students. The largest month-to-month change was a rise of 15 students, between May and June.

chart.title: Students completing a library research lesson (students; fictional data)

tasks.prompt: The chart shows the number of students completing a library research lesson at six fictional centres in the same study month. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料：完成圖書館資料搜尋課的學生數，比較同一個月六個中心的數字。寫至少 150 字：改寫圖表資訊、用一段說整體重點，再用數字支持比較。不要猜原因或把練習數字當成真實統計。
tasks.sample:
The chart presents the number of students completing a library research lesson at six fictional centres in the same study month. It allows a comparison of the reported counts, with each figure expressed in students.

Overall, the largest figure belonged to Centre A, whereas Centre F had the smallest. These are comparisons between centres, rather than changes over time.

Looking first at Centres A, B and C, the figures were 79, 76 and 75 students, respectively. Together, these three centres accounted for 230 students. Centre B recorded 3 fewer students than Centre A.

The remaining centres, D, E and F, recorded 54, 51 and 48 students, respectively. Their combined figure was 153 students, compared with 230 for the first group. Across all six centres, the total was 383 students. The last three centres therefore accounted for about 40 percent of the sum, with the other centres accounting for the remainder. The difference between the highest and lowest figures was 31 students.
