tasks.prompt: The table shows the average waiting time at three fictional clinics in 2022 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：三家診所 2022 年和 2024 年的平均候診時間。寫至少 150 字：改寫題目、用一段說最明顯的差別，再挑重要的數字比較；不用每個數字都寫，也不要猜原因。

chart.title: Average waiting time (minutes; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table compares the average time that patients waited at three fictional clinics in 2022 and 2024. All figures are given in minutes.

Overall, Clinic B had the longest waiting time in both years, whereas Clinic C had the shortest. Waiting times fell at Clinics A and B, but they rose very slightly at Clinic C.

In 2022, patients at Clinic B waited 42 minutes on average, compared with 35 minutes at Clinic A and only 18 minutes at Clinic C. The gap between the longest and the shortest wait was therefore 24 minutes.

By 2024, the situation had changed. The biggest improvement was at Clinic A, where the average wait dropped by 15 minutes to 20 minutes. Clinic B also improved, but only by 4 minutes, so it remained the slowest clinic at 38 minutes. In contrast, the figure for Clinic C went up by just 1 minute to 19 minutes, which was still the shortest wait of the three. As a result, the difference between the clinics narrowed to 19 minutes.

tasks.prompt: The table shows the average number of students using four study spaces per day on weekdays and at weekends at a fictional university. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：四個讀書空間平日和週末每天平均有多少學生使用。寫至少 150 字：先說平日和週末最大的不同，再比較數字。

chart.title: Students using study spaces per day (average; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table shows how many students used four different study spaces each day, on average, on weekdays and at weekends at a fictional university.

Overall, the library was by far the busiest space on weekdays, but at weekends the dormitory study room attracted the most students. Use of the library and the computer lab fell sharply at weekends, whereas the other two spaces became slightly busier.

On weekdays, the library had 220 users a day. The computer lab was the second most popular space with 140 students, while the dormitory study room and the café seating area were much quieter, with 60 and 45 users respectively.

At weekends, the pattern was very different. The number of library users dropped to 90, less than half of the weekday figure, and the computer lab fell even more steeply, from 140 to just 30 students. By contrast, the dormitory study room gained 35 users and reached 95, which made it the most popular space at weekends. The café seating area also rose a little, by 5 students to 50.

tasks.prompt: The table shows the percentage of first-year and third-year nursing students at a fictional school who did different types of weekly exercise (students could choose more than one type). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：一年級和三年級護理系學生每週做哪些運動（可複選）的百分比。寫至少 150 字：比較兩個年級，挑出最常見、變多和變少的。

chart.title: Weekly exercise of nursing students (% of students; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table compares the kinds of exercise that first-year and third-year nursing students at a fictional school did each week. The figures are percentages, and students could choose more than one activity.

Overall, walking was the most common form of exercise in both year groups. However, third-year students were less likely to walk, run or swim, and more of them used the gym or did no regular exercise at all.

Walking was reported by 62% of first-year students, compared with 48% of third-year students, a difference of 14 percentage points. Running followed the same pattern, falling from 25% to 18%, while swimming was the least popular activity in both groups, at 12% and 9%.

The only activity that became more popular was gym training. It was chosen by 20% of first-year students but by 31% of third-year students, an increase of 11 points, which made it the second most common activity among older students. Meanwhile, the proportion of students who did no regular exercise rose from 15% to 22%.

tasks.prompt: The table shows the number of meals of four types sold in a fictional hospital canteen in two weeks. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：醫院餐廳兩週內四種餐點的銷售份數。寫至少 150 字：說哪一種最多、哪些增加或減少，必要時算總數比較。

chart.title: Meals sold in a hospital canteen (meals; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table gives the number of meals of four different types that a fictional hospital canteen sold over two weeks.

Overall, rice boxes were the best-selling meal in both weeks, although their sales fell slightly. Noodle soup and salad became more popular, while sandwich sales hardly changed. In total, the canteen sold 970 meals in the first week and 1,030 in the second, an increase of 60.

In the first week, 410 rice boxes were sold, which was clearly more than any other option. Noodle soup came second with 260 meals, followed by sandwiches at 180, and salad was the least popular choice at 120.

In the second week, rice box sales dropped by 30 to 380. In contrast, noodle soup sales rose by 50 to 310, which was the largest increase in number, and salad sales grew from 120 to 165 meals, a rise of 45. Sandwich sales stayed almost the same, falling by only 5 to 175. As a result, salad was still the least popular meal, but it was only 10 meals behind sandwiches in the second week.

tasks.prompt: The table shows the average number of hours that students in four year groups at a fictional nursing school slept each night in normal weeks and in examination weeks. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：四個年級的學生平常週和考試週平均每晚睡幾小時。寫至少 150 字：說所有年級共同的變化，再比較減少最多和最少的。

chart.title: Average sleep per night (hours; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table shows how many hours students in four year groups at a fictional nursing school slept each night, on average, in normal weeks and in examination weeks.

Overall, every year group slept less during examination weeks. Year 2 students experienced the largest fall and had the least sleep during exams, while Year 1 students slept the longest in normal weeks.

In normal weeks, the figures ranged from 6.5 to 7.2 hours. Year 1 students slept the most, at 7.2 hours a night, followed by Year 4 at 6.9 hours and Year 2 at 6.8 hours. Year 3 students had the shortest sleep, at 6.5 hours.

During examination weeks, all four figures dropped. The biggest decrease was in Year 2, where sleep fell by 1.4 hours to just 5.4 hours, the lowest figure in the table. Year 1 students lost 1.1 hours and slept 6.1 hours. By comparison, the changes for Years 3 and 4 were smaller, with each group losing 0.6 hours, so Year 4 students had the most sleep in examination weeks, at 6.3 hours.

tasks.prompt: The table shows the results of 100 hand-hygiene checks on each of four wards in a fictional hospital in one month. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：四個病房各 100 次手部衛生稽核的通過和未通過次數。寫至少 150 字：說整體情況，再比較最好和最需要改進的病房。

chart.title: Hand-hygiene checks in one month (number of checks; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table presents the results of hand-hygiene checks carried out on four wards of a fictional hospital during one month. Each ward was checked 100 times.

Overall, the large majority of checks were passed on every ward. Ward 4 had the best results, while Ward 2 had the highest number of failed checks by a clear margin.

Ward 4 passed 95 of its 100 checks, which meant that only 5 checks were failed. Ward 1 was not far behind, with 92 passes and 8 failures, and Ward 3 also performed well, passing 88 checks and failing 12.

Ward 2, however, stood out from the others. It passed 76 checks and failed 24, which was almost five times as many failures as Ward 4 and twice as many as Ward 3. The difference between the best and the weakest ward was therefore 19 passed checks. Taken together, the four wards passed 351 of the 400 checks and failed 49, so almost half of all the failures came from a single ward.

tasks.prompt: The table shows the ways in which students at a fictional nursing school travelled to school in 2019 and 2024. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：學生上學方式的百分比，比較 2019 年和 2024 年。寫至少 150 字：說最常見的方式和最大的變化，再用數字支持。

chart.title: How students travelled to school (% of students; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table compares the percentages of students at a fictional nursing school who used five different ways of travelling to school in 2019 and 2024.

Overall, the bus and the scooter remained the two most common choices, but both became less popular. Cycling showed the most dramatic change, more than doubling over the period, and walking and travelling by car also increased slightly.

In 2019, 38% of students took the bus and 34% rode a scooter, so these two methods together accounted for 72% of all journeys. By 2024, the bus had fallen to 30% and the scooter to 28%, and their combined share had dropped to 58%.

The other three methods grew. The proportion of students who cycled rose from 8% to 17%, which made the bicycle the third most common way of getting to school. Walking increased by 2 percentage points to 14%, while the share of students travelling by car went up from 8% to 11%. As a result, the gap between the least and most popular methods became narrower.

tasks.prompt: The table shows how many nursing students in three fictional classes passed three skills tests on their first attempt (each class has 34 students). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：三個班（每班 34 人）三項技術考第一次就通過的人數。寫至少 150 字：比較三項技術，也注意哪一班和其他班不一樣。

chart.title: Students passing skills tests on the first attempt (out of 34 per class; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table shows how many students in three fictional nursing classes passed three practical skills tests at their first attempt. Each class had 34 students.

Overall, hand hygiene was the skill that the most students passed in every class, while wound dressing generally had the lowest results. Class B was the main exception to this pattern.

Hand hygiene results were high and very similar across the three classes, at 32, 31 and 33 students for Classes A, B and C. Blood pressure measurement came next in Classes A and C, with 28 and 30 students passing, but only 25 students in Class B passed this test.

Wound dressing produced the widest differences. Just 20 students in Class A and 18 in Class C passed it, which were the two lowest figures in the table. In Class B, however, 26 students passed wound dressing, slightly more than the 25 who passed blood pressure measurement. In other words, Class B was weaker than the other classes at measuring blood pressure but clearly stronger at dressing wounds, with 8 more passes than Class C.

tasks.prompt: The table shows the monthly spending of a fictional nursing student in two semesters, in New Taiwan dollars. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：一位學生兩個學期每月花在五個項目的錢（新台幣）。寫至少 150 字：說最大的支出和整體變化，再比較增加和減少的項目。

chart.title: Monthly spending of a student (NT$; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table shows how much a fictional nursing student spent each month on five types of expense during two semesters. All amounts are in New Taiwan dollars.

Overall, food was by far the largest expense in both semesters, and it increased. Spending on transport and on books and printing went down, leisure spending rose, and the phone bill stayed the same. The student's total monthly spending increased only slightly, from NT$11,600 to NT$11,900.

In the first semester, the student spent NT$6,500 a month on food, which was more than all the other categories combined. Books and printing cost NT$1,800, leisure NT$1,500 and transport NT$1,200, while the phone was the smallest item at NT$600.

In the second semester, food spending grew by NT$700 to NT$7,200, and leisure spending went up by NT$600 to NT$2,100. These increases were balanced by lower costs elsewhere. Books and printing fell by NT$700 to NT$1,100, and transport dropped from NT$1,200 to NT$900. As a result, the total rose by just NT$300.

tasks.prompt: The table shows patients' average satisfaction scores, out of 10, for four services at a fictional hospital in 2023 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
tasks.zh: 教學模擬資料（表格）：病人對四項服務的平均滿意度（滿分 10），比較 2023 年和 2025 年。寫至少 150 字：說最高、最低和進步最多的項目。

chart.title: Patients' satisfaction scores (out of 10; fictional data)

tasks.sample:
The table compares patients' average satisfaction scores for four services at a fictional hospital in 2023 and 2025. The scores are out of 10.

Overall, every service received a higher score in 2025 than in 2023. Nursing care was rated the highest in both years, whereas meals received the lowest scores. The largest improvements were in discharge information and admission.

In 2023, nursing care already scored 8.4, well above the other services. Admission was rated 6.8, while discharge information and meals were the two weakest areas, with scores of 6.1 and 5.9 respectively.

By 2025, discharge information had improved the most, rising by 1.4 points to 7.5. Admission also showed a clear rise of 1.1 points and reached 7.9, which made it the second highest score. By contrast, the changes for nursing care and meals were small. Nursing care went up by 0.2 to 8.6, and meals increased by only 0.3 to 6.2, so meals remained well behind the other three services.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how reusable medical instruments are prepared for use again in a fictional hospital. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化的教學流程）：可重複使用的醫療器械怎麼處理後再使用。寫至少 150 字：總覽說幾個步驟、從哪裡開始到哪裡結束，再照順序寫每個主要步驟（多用被動語態）。實際作業依各院的規範。

chart.title: Preparing reusable instruments for use again (simplified)
steps: Collect used instruments in closed containers
Pack in sterilisation wraps and label
Store sterile packs in a clean, dry area
Check packs and send them to the ward

tasks.sample:
The diagram illustrates the steps that a fictional hospital follows to prepare reusable medical instruments so that they can be used again.

Overall, the process consists of seven stages. It begins with the collection of used instruments and ends when sterile packs are sent back to the wards. Cleaning, packing and sterilisation take place in the middle of the process.

First, used instruments are collected in closed containers. They are then cleaned in order to remove blood and tissue. After cleaning, each item is inspected and dried, so that any damaged or dirty instrument can be found before the next stage. Next, the instruments are packed in special sterilisation wraps and labelled.

Once the packs are ready, they are sterilised in a steam steriliser. After that, the sterile packs are stored in a clean, dry area, where they stay until they are needed. Finally, when a ward requests them, the packs are checked once more and sent to the ward, which completes the cycle and allows the instruments to be used for patients again.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how a blood sample is processed in a fictional hospital, from the doctor's order to the result. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化的教學流程）：血液檢體從醫師開單到報告送回的流程。寫至少 150 字：總覽說一共幾步、起點和終點，再分兩段照順序寫。

chart.title: Processing a blood sample (simplified)
steps: Nurse checks the patient's identity and takes the sample
Label the tube at the bedside
Send the sample to the laboratory
Results sent to the doctor's computer

tasks.sample:
The diagram shows the stages involved in processing a blood sample in a fictional hospital, from the moment a test is ordered until the result reaches the doctor.

Overall, there are eight steps in the process. The first three take place on the ward, three more are carried out in the laboratory after the sample arrives, and the process ends when the results are sent electronically to the doctor.

The process starts when a doctor orders a blood test. A nurse then checks the patient's identity and takes the blood sample. Immediately afterwards, the tube is labelled at the bedside, so that the sample cannot be confused with another patient's. When this has been done, the sample is sent to the laboratory.

On arrival, the sample is registered and checked. It is then tested by an analyser, which produces the results. Before anything is released, laboratory staff check these results carefully. In the final stage, the results are sent to the doctor's computer, where they can be read and used to make decisions about the patient's care.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how rainwater is collected and used on a fictional university campus. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖：校園收集雨水再利用的流程。寫至少 150 字：總覽說幾個步驟、從下雨到最後用在哪裡，再照順序描述。

chart.title: Collecting and using rainwater on a campus
steps: Gutters carry water to a downpipe
Pump to a smaller tank on the roof

tasks.sample:
The diagram explains how rainwater is collected and reused on a fictional university campus.

Overall, the system has six main stages. It begins when rain falls on the roof of a building and ends when the stored water is used for flushing toilets and watering plants. Along the way, the water is filtered, stored and pumped.

To begin with, rain falls on the roof of a building and runs into the gutters. These gutters carry the water to a downpipe. Before the water goes any further, it passes through a filter, which removes leaves and dirt. The cleaned water is then stored in a large underground tank.

When the water is needed, a pump moves it from the underground tank to a smaller tank on the roof. From there, the water is supplied to the building. In the last stage, it is used to flush toilets and to water the plants on the campus. As a result, the system reuses rain for purposes that do not require drinking water.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how used paper is recycled to make new paper. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化）：廢紙回收做成新紙的流程。寫至少 150 字：總覽說一共幾個步驟、起點和終點，再照順序寫（多用被動語態）。

chart.title: Recycling used paper (simplified)
steps: Mixing with water to make pulp
Cleaning and pressing into thin sheets

tasks.sample:
The diagram shows the process by which used paper is recycled and made into new paper.

Overall, there are seven stages in the process. It starts with the collection of used paper from recycling bins and finishes with new paper being cut and packed. The most important change takes place in the middle stages, when the old paper is turned into pulp.

First of all, used paper is collected from recycling bins. It is then sorted according to its type and quality. In the third stage, the sorted paper is mixed with water, and this produces a soft pulp. Next, ink and pieces of plastic are removed from the pulp.

After that, the pulp is cleaned and pressed into thin sheets. These sheets are then dried as they pass over heated rollers. In the final step, the new paper is cut to the right size and packed, ready to be sold and used again. In this way, paper that has been thrown away becomes a useful product once more.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how a medicine is given to a patient on a hospital ward (simplified). Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化的教學流程）：病房給藥從開立處方到觀察副作用。寫至少 150 字：總覽說幾個步驟、誰參與，再照順序寫。實際給藥依學校和醫院的完整規範。

chart.title: Giving a medicine on a ward (simplified)
steps: Pharmacist checks and prepares the medicine
Nurse checks: right patient, medicine, dose, route, time
Nurse explains and gives the medicine

tasks.sample:
The diagram illustrates the main steps in giving a medicine to a patient on a hospital ward.

Overall, the process has seven stages and involves three members of the health care team. A doctor and a pharmacist are responsible for the first two steps, while the nurse carries out most of the remaining stages, ending with observation of the patient.

The process begins when the doctor writes a prescription. A pharmacist then checks it and prepares the medicine, which is sent to the ward. Before giving anything, the nurse checks five things: the right patient, the right medicine, the right dose, the right route and the right time.

Once these checks are complete, the nurse explains the medicine to the patient and gives it. Straight afterwards, the dose is recorded, so that other staff know exactly what the patient has received. In the final stage, the nurse watches the patient for any side effects. This last step shows that the process does not finish when the medicine has been given.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows the life cycle of an Aedes mosquito. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖：埃及斑蚊（Aedes）的生命週期，依美國 CDC 的說明簡化。寫至少 150 字：總覽說有幾個階段、哪些在水裡，再照順序描述；這是一個循環。

chart.title: The life cycle of an Aedes mosquito (about 7–10 days from egg to adult)
steps: Eggs laid on the inside wall of a container, just above the water
Water covers the eggs: larvae hatch
Larvae live and grow in the water
Pupae: live in the water, do not eat
Adults come out and fly away
Female bites for blood to produce eggs

tasks.sample:
The diagram shows the life cycle of an Aedes mosquito, which takes about seven to ten days from egg to adult.

Overall, the mosquito passes through four forms: egg, larva, pupa and adult. Most of its early development takes place in water, and the cycle starts again when a female adult lays new eggs.

The cycle begins when a female mosquito lays her eggs on the inside wall of a container, just above the surface of the water. When water rises and covers them, the eggs hatch into larvae. The larvae live in the water, where they feed and grow.

In the next stage, the larvae change into pupae. Like the larvae, the pupae live in the water, but unlike them, they do not eat. After this stage, adult mosquitoes come out of the pupae and fly away. Finally, a female mosquito bites a person or an animal, because she needs blood in order to produce eggs. She then lays her eggs, and the whole cycle is repeated.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how meals are prepared and delivered to patients in a fictional hospital. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化的教學流程）：醫院病人餐從規劃菜單到送餐前核對。寫至少 150 字：總覽說幾個步驟、在哪些地方進行，再照順序寫。

chart.title: Preparing and delivering patients' meals (simplified)
steps: Dietitians plan menus for different diets
Trays checked and put in heated trolleys
Tray checked against the patient's name, then served

tasks.sample:
The diagram outlines how a fictional hospital prepares meals and delivers them to its patients.

Overall, the process is made up of seven steps. It begins with dietitians planning menus and ends on the ward, where each tray is checked before it is served. Checking takes place at more than one stage, which reduces the risk of a patient receiving the wrong meal.

First, dietitians plan menus for different diets. Patients then choose their meals from these menus, and their orders are sent to the kitchen. In the kitchen, the meals are cooked and labelled with each patient's name and type of diet.

After cooking, the trays are checked and placed in heated trolleys, which keep the food warm. These trolleys are then taken to the wards. In the final stage, a member of staff compares each tray with the patient's name before serving it. Only when the name and the meal match is the tray given to the patient, so the process ends with a safety check rather than with cooking.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how a new patient is seen at a fictional community clinic. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化的教學流程）：社區診所新病人從預約到約下次回診。寫至少 150 字：總覽說幾個步驟、起點和終點，再分兩段照順序寫。

chart.title: A first visit to a community clinic (simplified)
steps: Arrive and check in at reception

tasks.sample:
The diagram shows the stages of a first visit to a fictional community clinic, from booking an appointment to arranging the next one.

Overall, the process has seven stages. The first two take place before the patient arrives, the next four happen at the clinic itself, and the process ends with a follow-up appointment if one is needed.

To start with, the patient books an appointment, either online or by phone. The clinic then sends a confirmation message. On the day of the appointment, the patient arrives and checks in at reception. A nurse then measures the patient's height, weight and blood pressure before the patient sees the doctor.

In the fifth stage, the doctor examines the patient. After the examination, the patient pays and receives a prescription. In the final stage, a follow-up appointment is booked, but only if the doctor thinks that another visit is necessary. This means that the process can end in two ways, depending on the patient's needs.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how plastic bottles are recycled. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化）：寶特瓶回收再製的流程。寫至少 150 字：總覽說一共幾個步驟、從收集到做成新產品，再照順序寫（多用被動語態）。

chart.title: Recycling plastic bottles (simplified)
steps: Collection and transport to a recycling centre

tasks.sample:
The diagram illustrates the process of recycling plastic bottles and turning them into new products.

Overall, there are six stages in the process. It begins with the collection of used bottles and ends when small plastic pellets are made into new items, such as clothing or new bottles. In between, the bottles are sorted, cleaned and broken down.

At the beginning of the process, used bottles are collected and taken to a recycling centre. There, they are sorted according to their type and colour. Next, the labels and caps are removed, because they are made of different materials from the bottles themselves.

After that, the bottles are washed and cut into small flakes. These flakes are then melted and formed into small pellets. In the last stage, the pellets are used as a raw material to make new products, for example clothing or new plastic bottles. In this way, an object that would otherwise become waste is changed into something useful.

tasks.prompt: The diagram shows how tea leaves are processed to make black tea. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.
tasks.zh: 流程圖（簡化）：紅茶從採茶到包裝的製程。寫至少 150 字：總覽說幾個步驟和茶葉的變化，再照順序描述。

chart.title: Making black tea (simplified)

tasks.sample:
The diagram shows the main stages in the production of black tea, from picking the leaves to packing the finished product.

Overall, the process involves six steps. During these stages, fresh green leaves gradually lose water and change colour until they become dry, dark tea that is ready to be sold.

First, the tea leaves are picked by hand. They are then spread out so that they can wither and lose some of their water. After this, the leaves are rolled, which breaks their surface. This prepares them for the most important change in the process.

In the fourth stage, the rolled leaves are left to oxidise, and during this time they turn dark. Next, the leaves are dried with hot air, which stops the change and removes most of the remaining water. Finally, the tea is sorted according to the size of the pieces and packed. At the end of the process, the leaves look very different from the fresh leaves that were picked at the beginning.

grammar.title: Task 1：先寫總覽，再用數據支持
points: 第一段用自己的話說圖表的對象、單位和時間，不要逐字照抄題目；overview（總覽）用一兩句說最大趨勢、最高最低或主要差別，不要只列數字，也不要加入個人意見或猜原因。
細節段挑關鍵數字比較：from…to… 寫起終點，by… 寫差額，higher／lower than 比高低；表格不用每格都寫，挑最高、最低和明顯差別，用 while／whereas、twice as many 對照。
The chart shows 用現在式介紹圖；描述已經發生的變化用過去式，例如 rose、fell、remained stable，全文時間要一致。
流程圖（process）：總覽說一共幾個步驟、從哪裡開始到哪裡結束；步驟多用被動語態（is collected、are washed），照順序用 First、Next、After that、Finally 連起來，每個主要步驟都要寫到。

examples.en: The chart shows the number of clinic visits from January to June.
examples.zh: 圖表呈現一到六月的診所看診人次。

examples.en: Overall, visits fell during the period.
examples.zh: 整體而言，這段期間的看診人次下降。

examples.en: The figure rose from 20 to 30.
examples.zh: 數字從 20 增加到 30。

examples.en: Clinic B had the longest wait in both years, whereas Clinic C had the shortest.
examples.zh: B 診所兩年的候診時間都最長，C 診所則最短。

examples.en: First, the instruments are cleaned. After that, they are packed and labelled.
examples.zh: 首先，器械會被清洗。接著，它們會被包裝並貼上標籤。

mistakes.bad: In my opinion, the clinic did a good job.
mistakes.good: Overall, the number of visits increased.
mistakes.why: Task 1 要描述圖表；圖上沒有提供經營表現，就不要自己評論。
rose 本身就是過去式動詞，前面不再加 was。

mistakes.bad: First, the bottles collect and take to a recycling centre.
mistakes.good: First, the bottles are collected and taken to a recycling centre.
mistakes.why: 瓶子不會自己收集，是「被收集」：流程圖的步驟大多用被動語態 be + 過去分詞。

stages.name: ⑫ 兩面意見的短文（Task 2 暖身）
stages.goal: 用四段簡單英文寫兩邊的理由，再說清楚自己的選擇。
criteria: 分四段：開頭、第一種看法、第二種看法、結尾
兩邊各有理由，至少有一個具體例子
用 On the one hand、On the other hand 或 However 表示轉換
結尾有自己的意見，不突然改立場，整題至少 150 字

grammar.title: 四段談兩邊：On the one hand…、On the other hand…
points: 開頭先用一兩句交代兩種看法，再讓讀者知道自己的立場；一段只做一件事。
On the one hand 放第一個主體段，接第一邊的理由和例子，不要只把題目重寫一次。
On the other hand 換另一邊；However 表示轉折，放新句句首時後面加逗號。
結尾用 In conclusion 收回重點；I agree that 後面接完整句子，I agree with 後面接人或看法。

examples.en: Some students like online classes, but others prefer classes at school.
examples.zh: 有些學生喜歡線上課，有些比較喜歡在學校上課。

examples.en: On the one hand, online classes save travel time.
examples.zh: 一方面，線上課省下交通時間。

examples.en: On the other hand, students need practice with a teacher.
examples.zh: 另一方面，學生需要在老師指導下練習。

examples.en: However, one method does not meet every need.
examples.zh: 不過，一種方法無法滿足所有需要。

examples.en: In conclusion, I agree that both methods are useful.
examples.zh: 總結來說，我同意兩種方法都有用。

mistakes.bad: I am agree that both methods are useful.
mistakes.good: I agree that both methods are useful.
mistakes.why: agree 本身就是動詞，不需要再加 am。

mistakes.bad: Online classes are useful, however, students need practice.
mistakes.good: Online classes are useful. However, students need practice.
mistakes.why: however 不能只靠逗號把兩個完整句子接起來；這裡先分成兩句。

tasks.prompt: Some nursing students like online classes. Others prefer classes at school. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 護理課適合線上上課，還是在學校上課？用四段寫兩邊的理由，再說自己的看法。training equipment＝練習器材；skills lesson＝技術練習課。
tasks.sample:
Some nursing students like online classes, but others prefer classes at school. I think both have useful points, and nursing schools should use them for different lessons.

On the one hand, online classes are useful for some study activities. Students can listen to an English lesson at home and read the notes on a computer. For example, I can review nursing words in my dormitory. I do not need to travel to school for this short practice, so I have time for other work.

On the other hand, practice at school is important. Students can use training equipment with a teacher and ask questions at once. For example, a teacher can check a student's hand position during a skills lesson. However, an online lesson does not offer the same practice.

In conclusion, I agree that online classes are useful for learning words and ideas. However, nursing students also need practice with teachers and equipment at school.

tasks.prompt: Some people want flexible hospital visiting hours. Others want fixed visiting hours. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 醫院探病時間應彈性，還是固定？用四段討論兩邊，最後說你的想法。這是意見練習，不是任何醫院的現行規定。flexible＝有彈性的；privacy＝隱私；permission＝同意。
tasks.sample:
Some people think hospital visiting hours should be flexible. Others think hospitals need fixed hours. I think visitors are important, but hospitals also need clear rules.

On the one hand, flexible hours help families with different schedules. A person sometimes finishes work late and misses a short visiting period. A flexible time gives this person a chance to visit. For example, a patient sometimes wants a family member nearby after a difficult day. The family also has time to ask questions with the patient's permission.

On the other hand, patients need rest, privacy, and time for care. Many visitors in one room can make it noisy. Staff also need space for their work. However, a fixed rule sometimes needs an exception for a patient's situation.

To sum up, I agree that hospitals should have clear visiting rules. They should also consider the patient's wishes and care needs. Staff and families can discuss a suitable visiting time together.

tasks.prompt: Some nursing students use phones during clinical practice. Others keep their phones away. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 護理學生實習時使用手機，有什麼好處和需要留意的地方？用四段寫兩邊，再說自己的立場。要尊重病人隱私並遵守實習單位規定。approved tools＝經單位核准的工具。
tasks.sample:
Some nursing students use phones during clinical practice, but others keep their phones away. I think phones can help with study, but patient care needs clear rules.

On the one hand, a phone is a useful study tool. A student can check an English word during a break. Students can also read learning materials that their teacher shares. For example, I use a dictionary on my phone after a lesson. It helps me understand a word in my notes.

On the other hand, a phone can take a student's attention away from other people. Messages and games interrupt work. Patient privacy is also important. Students should not take patient photos on a personal phone. However, they can ask their teacher about safe ways to use approved tools.

All things considered, I agree that phones have useful learning functions. However, nursing students should follow the hospital's rules and use their phones only at suitable times. Patient care and privacy come first.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer studying in a small group. Others prefer studying alone. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：讀書會與自己讀書。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about study groups. Some prefer studying in a small group, but others favour studying alone. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, group members explain difficult ideas to one another. A student notices a missing step during a practice explanation, so the speaker checks the textbook again. For example, three classmates compare their notes after a lesson. Each person brings a different question to the meeting.

On the other hand, studying alone gives a learner control over the pace. One student needs extra time for English vocabulary, but another already knows those words. A group sometimes moves too quickly or spends the whole meeting discussing one person's difficulty. Quiet individual review also avoids unnecessary conversation.

On balance, I prefer a short group meeting after individual preparation. Both activities have a clear purpose, so neither one needs to replace the other.

tasks.prompt: Some people think that studying in a small group should be the standard approach for everyone. Others think people should choose between studying in a small group and studying alone. Write four paragraphs about a common rule and a flexible choice, and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：讀書會與自己讀書。這題練「全部統一規定」和「保留個人選擇」的差別，不能只列出兩種工具。四段寫支持共同規則的理由、規則的限制與例子，再表明立場；至少150字。
tasks.sample:
There is a debate about whether studying in a small group should become the standard choice. Some people want one common approach, but others prefer more flexibility. I think a clear plan needs to respect different circumstances.

On the one hand, supporters of a common approach see useful benefits. Group members explain difficult ideas to one another. A student notices a missing step during a practice explanation, so the speaker checks the textbook again. For example, three classmates compare their notes after a lesson. Each person brings a different question to the meeting.

On the other hand, a single rule does not fit every situation. Studying alone gives a learner control over the pace. One student needs extra time for English vocabulary, but another already knows those words. A group sometimes moves too quickly or spends the whole meeting discussing one person's difficulty. Quiet individual review also avoids unnecessary conversation.

Overall, I prefer a short group meeting after individual preparation. Both activities have a clear purpose, so neither one needs to replace the other.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer using recorded lectures for review. Others prefer attending every review session in person. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：課堂錄影與現場聽課。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about lecture recordings. Some prefer using recorded lectures for review, but others favour attending every review session in person. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a recording allows a student to listen to an explanation again. A learner can pause at an unfamiliar word and look it up. For example, a nursing student reviews a lesson after an early placement day and writes down two questions for the next class.

On the other hand, a live review session gives students a chance to ask questions immediately. The teacher notices confusion and explains an idea in a different way. A recording alone does not answer a new question. Students also need a quiet place and a suitable device to use recordings.

Taking both views into account, I support recordings as an extra resource. Live opportunities to ask questions should remain available, especially for difficult practical topics.

tasks.prompt: Some people think that using recorded lectures for review should be the standard approach for everyone. Others think people should choose between using recorded lectures for review and attending every review session in person. Write four paragraphs about a common rule and a flexible choice, and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：課堂錄影與現場聽課。這題練「全部統一規定」和「保留個人選擇」的差別，不能只列出兩種工具。四段寫支持共同規則的理由、規則的限制與例子，再表明立場；至少150字。
tasks.sample:
There is a debate about whether using recorded lectures for review should become the standard choice. Some people want one common approach, but others prefer more flexibility. I think a clear plan needs to respect different circumstances.

On the one hand, supporters of a common approach see useful benefits. A recording allows a student to listen to an explanation again. A learner can pause at an unfamiliar word and look it up. For example, a nursing student reviews a lesson after an early placement day and writes down two questions for the next class.

On the other hand, a single rule does not fit every situation. A live review session gives students a chance to ask questions immediately. The teacher notices confusion and explains an idea in a different way. A recording alone does not answer a new question. Students also need a quiet place and a suitable device to use recordings.

In conclusion, I support recordings as an extra resource. Live opportunities to ask questions should remain available, especially for difficult practical topics.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer digital vocabulary cards. Others prefer paper vocabulary cards. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：電子與紙本單字卡。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about digital vocabulary cards. Some prefer digital vocabulary cards, but others favour paper vocabulary cards. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, digital cards are easy to carry on a phone. A student can hear a word and review a few cards during a bus journey. For example, the learner checks the pronunciation of a nursing word before a speaking practice. The cards also fit into short breaks.

On the other hand, paper cards offer a simple activity without messages or other apps on the screen. A student can spread difficult cards across a desk and sort them by topic. A phone battery sometimes runs out during travel. Some learners also prefer writing a word with a pen.

To sum up, I think students should choose a method they use regularly. A small set of paper cards is also a useful backup for digital study.

tasks.prompt: Some people think that digital vocabulary cards should be the standard approach for everyone. Others think people should choose between digital vocabulary cards and paper vocabulary cards. Write four paragraphs about a common rule and a flexible choice, and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：電子與紙本單字卡。這題練「全部統一規定」和「保留個人選擇」的差別，不能只列出兩種工具。四段寫支持共同規則的理由、規則的限制與例子，再表明立場；至少150字。
tasks.sample:
There is a debate about whether digital vocabulary cards should become the standard choice. Some people want one common approach, but others prefer more flexibility. I think a clear plan needs to respect different circumstances.

On the one hand, supporters of a common approach see useful benefits. Digital cards are easy to carry on a phone. A student can hear a word and review a few cards during a bus journey. For example, the learner checks the pronunciation of a nursing word before a speaking practice. The cards also fit into short breaks.

On the other hand, a single rule does not fit every situation. Paper cards offer a simple activity without messages or other apps on the screen. A student can spread difficult cards across a desk and sort them by topic. A phone battery sometimes runs out during travel. Some learners also prefer writing a word with a pen.

All things considered, I think students should choose a method they use regularly. A small set of paper cards is also a useful backup for digital study.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer keeping a campus library open later. Others prefer concentrating library services in daytime hours. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：延長圖書館時間與維持日間服務。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about library opening hours. Some prefer keeping a campus library open later, but others favour concentrating library services in daytime hours. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, later opening hours give students another place to study after class. A nursing student with a daytime placement may reach campus in the evening. For example, the student uses a quiet desk to finish a reading task before returning to a shared dormitory room.

On the other hand, longer hours require staff, lighting and a safe way to enter the building. A nearly empty building still uses resources. Some students also need help from specialist library staff during the day. Moving resources to late hours could reduce support at the busiest times.

On balance, I support a small late study area and clear daytime help hours. The whole library does not need identical opening times.

tasks.prompt: Some people think that keeping a campus library open later should be the standard approach for everyone. Others think people should choose between keeping a campus library open later and concentrating library services in daytime hours. Write four paragraphs about a common rule and a flexible choice, and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：延長圖書館時間與維持日間服務。這題練「全部統一規定」和「保留個人選擇」的差別，不能只列出兩種工具。四段寫支持共同規則的理由、規則的限制與例子，再表明立場；至少150字。
tasks.sample:
There is a debate about whether keeping a campus library open later should become the standard choice. Some people want one common approach, but others prefer more flexibility. I think a clear plan needs to respect different circumstances.

On the one hand, supporters of a common approach see useful benefits. Later opening hours give students another place to study after class. A nursing student with a daytime placement may reach campus in the evening. For example, the student uses a quiet desk to finish a reading task before returning to a shared dormitory room.

On the other hand, a single rule does not fit every situation. Longer hours require staff, lighting and a safe way to enter the building. A nearly empty building still uses resources. Some students also need help from specialist library staff during the day. Moving resources to late hours could reduce support at the busiest times.

Overall, I support a small late study area and clear daytime help hours. The whole library does not need identical opening times.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer support from a student mentor. Others prefer individual meetings with a teacher. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：學長姐陪伴與教師個別協助。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about peer mentoring. Some prefer support from a student mentor, but others favour individual meetings with a teacher. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a student mentor remembers the practical questions from the first year. A new student can ask where to find a classroom or how to prepare for a laboratory lesson. For example, a short campus tour makes the first week feel less confusing and starts a friendly conversation.

On the other hand, a teacher understands formal course requirements and can deal with academic concerns. A student mentor may not know the answer to a complicated question. Personal experiences also differ. New students need a clear way to contact staff instead of treating another student's advice as an official rule.

Taking both views into account, I support student mentors for everyday guidance, with staff available for formal questions. The roles should be clear to everyone.

tasks.prompt: Some people think that support from a student mentor should be the standard approach for everyone. Others think people should choose between support from a student mentor and individual meetings with a teacher. Write four paragraphs about a common rule and a flexible choice, and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：學長姐陪伴與教師個別協助。這題練「全部統一規定」和「保留個人選擇」的差別，不能只列出兩種工具。四段寫支持共同規則的理由、規則的限制與例子，再表明立場；至少150字。
tasks.sample:
There is a debate about whether support from a student mentor should become the standard choice. Some people want one common approach, but others prefer more flexibility. I think a clear plan needs to respect different circumstances.

On the one hand, supporters of a common approach see useful benefits. A student mentor remembers the practical questions from the first year. A new student can ask where to find a classroom or how to prepare for a laboratory lesson. For example, a short campus tour makes the first week feel less confusing and starts a friendly conversation.

On the other hand, a single rule does not fit every situation. A teacher understands formal course requirements and can deal with academic concerns. A student mentor may not know the answer to a complicated question. Personal experiences also differ. New students need a clear way to contact staff instead of treating another student's advice as an official rule.

In conclusion, I support student mentors for everyday guidance, with staff available for formal questions. The roles should be clear to everyone.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer writing a short reflection after each placement day. Others prefer writing one longer reflection at the end of the week. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：每次寫反思與每週整理。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about clinical learning journals. Some prefer writing a short reflection after each placement day, but others favour writing one longer reflection at the end of the week. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a short daily reflection helps a student remember a learning question. The learner records a general communication challenge without including patient details. For example, a student writes about feeling nervous during an introduction and practises a clearer opening sentence before the next day.

On the other hand, a weekly reflection gives more time to connect several experiences. Students can compare their confidence at the start and end of a week. A long daily writing requirement adds work after a tiring day. Repeated summaries may also say little about the next learning step.

To sum up, I prefer a few private daily learning notes followed by one thoughtful weekly reflection. Patient information does not belong in personal study notes.

tasks.prompt: Some people think that writing a short reflection after each placement day should be the standard approach for everyone. Others think people should choose between writing a short reflection after each placement day and writing one longer reflection at the end of the week. Write four paragraphs about a common rule and a flexible choice, and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：每次寫反思與每週整理。這題練「全部統一規定」和「保留個人選擇」的差別，不能只列出兩種工具。四段寫支持共同規則的理由、規則的限制與例子，再表明立場；至少150字。
tasks.sample:
There is a debate about whether writing a short reflection after each placement day should become the standard choice. Some people want one common approach, but others prefer more flexibility. I think a clear plan needs to respect different circumstances.

On the one hand, supporters of a common approach see useful benefits. A short daily reflection helps a student remember a learning question. The learner records a general communication challenge without including patient details. For example, a student writes about feeling nervous during an introduction and practises a clearer opening sentence before the next day.

On the other hand, a single rule does not fit every situation. A weekly reflection gives more time to connect several experiences. Students can compare their confidence at the start and end of a week. A long daily writing requirement adds work after a tiring day. Repeated summaries may also say little about the next learning step.

All things considered, I prefer a few private daily learning notes followed by one thoughtful weekly reflection. Patient information does not belong in personal study notes.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer receiving comments after every writing exercise. Others prefer receiving a weekly summary of writing feedback. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.

tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about teacher feedback schedules. Some prefer receiving comments after every writing exercise, but others favour receiving a weekly summary of writing feedback. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, quick comments help a learner connect feedback with a recent answer. The student still remembers the intended meaning and can try a correction at once. For example, a teacher points out one missing verb, and the learner rewrites the sentence before practising another example.

On the other hand, a weekly summary can show a repeated difficulty across several exercises. The teacher has time to choose the most useful examples and explain one pattern carefully. Immediate comments on every line may feel overwhelming. Teachers also need time to prepare lessons and help other students.

On balance, I support quick feedback on the main problem and a weekly review of patterns. The aim is a usable next step, not a page full of corrections.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer more supervised simulation practice. Others prefer more observation during clinical placements. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.

tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about simulation practice. Some prefer more supervised simulation practice, but others favour more observation during clinical placements. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a simulation gives students a place to practise a defined task with a teacher. The group can pause and discuss a communication problem. For example, a student repeats an introduction to a simulated patient after feedback. The teacher can adjust the difficulty to the class.

On the other hand, clinical observation shows how staff work with real people in a busy setting. Students see different roles and hear questions that do not appear in a simple classroom script. Simulation equipment and teacher time also cost money. Neither setting can include every possible situation.

Taking both views into account, I think both settings have a place. Students need preparation and supervision, with clear learning goals for simulation and placement activities.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer practising English with one regular partner. Others prefer changing partners frequently. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：固定語伴與輪流換語伴。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about English learning partners. Some prefer practising English with one regular partner, but others favour changing partners frequently. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a regular partner becomes familiar with a learner's goals. The pair can notice progress and return to a difficult topic. For example, two nursing students practise introducing themselves in the first week and try a longer conversation later. A familiar person may make speaking feel easier.

On the other hand, new partners bring different questions and speaking habits. A learner needs to understand more than one familiar voice. Working with the same person all term may also be difficult when schedules change. One student may talk much more than the other unless the activity is organised carefully.

To sum up, I prefer a regular partner for some sessions and new partners for others. Both familiarity and variety are useful parts of speaking practice.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer frequent full practice examinations. Others prefer short practice tasks between occasional full examinations. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：頻繁模擬考與分段練習。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about practice examinations. Some prefer frequent full practice examinations, but others favour short practice tasks between occasional full examinations. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a full practice examination lets students experience timing and several tasks together. A nursing student preparing for IELTS can notice how much time a long essay needs. For example, the student learns to leave a few minutes for checking rather than using the whole period on an introduction.

On the other hand, short tasks give learners time to work on one weakness. A student can practise writing an overview or developing a reason without completing a whole test. Frequent long examinations use much of the available study time. Repeating a test does not automatically explain why an answer needs improvement.

On balance, I prefer focused practice most weeks and full examinations at planned intervals. The results should guide the next lesson instead of becoming the only activity.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer giving a short oral presentation. Others prefer submitting a written report. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：口頭簡報與書面報告。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about presentation formats. Some prefer giving a short oral presentation, but others favour submitting a written report. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, an oral presentation asks students to explain an idea clearly to listeners. Questions show which parts need another explanation. For example, a student introduces a community service in simple English and answers a classmate's question about its location. This creates practice for organised speaking.

On the other hand, a written report allows more careful checking of sources and wording. Some subjects need detailed comparisons that are difficult to follow in a short talk. Presentations also take class time, and speaking anxiety can hide a student's understanding. The assessment needs a clear purpose.

Taking both views into account, I support both formats across a course. The format should match the skill being practised rather than forcing every assignment into the same form.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer following a fixed daily study timetable. Others prefer adjusting study tasks each day. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：固定讀書表與彈性安排。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about study planning. Some prefer following a fixed daily study timetable, but others favour adjusting study tasks each day. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a fixed timetable reduces the number of decisions before studying. A learner knows when to open the vocabulary cards and when to write a short paragraph. For example, a student reviews English after breakfast on ordinary school days and develops a regular starting habit.

On the other hand, clinical placements, examinations and family responsibilities change the time available. A rigid timetable may become unrealistic during a busy week. Students also need more time for some topics than others. A plan should help organise work rather than create guilt about every unexpected change.

To sum up, I prefer a regular starting time with flexible task sizes. A smaller activity on a busy day can keep the routine realistic.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer using campus computers for coursework. Others prefer using personal devices for coursework. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：公共電腦與個人設備。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about campus computers. Some prefer using campus computers for coursework, but others favour using personal devices for coursework. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, campus computers give students access to common software without requiring a new personal device. A learner can complete an assignment even when a home computer is unavailable. For example, a nursing student uses a library computer to format a presentation and check the course website.

On the other hand, personal devices allow students to work at convenient times and save their preferred settings. Campus rooms may be busy just before a deadline. Maintaining many shared computers also requires staff and money. Students still need accessible ways to use files and protect their account information.

On balance, I support dependable shared computers alongside personal devices. Access to coursework should not depend on owning an expensive machine.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer using only English during nursing language lessons. Others prefer using Chinese explanations alongside English. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：雙語說明與全英語課堂。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about bilingual nursing lessons. Some prefer using only English during nursing language lessons, but others favour using Chinese explanations alongside English. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, English throughout a lesson gives learners repeated opportunities to listen and respond. Familiar classroom instructions become easier with practice. For example, students learn to ask for a word to be repeated and then use the same request during a conversation activity.

On the other hand, a brief Chinese explanation can clarify a difficult meaning for a beginner. Without that support, a learner may repeat a sentence without understanding it. Nursing terms can be unfamiliar in both languages. A class also contains students with different levels of English experience.

Taking both views into account, I prefer mostly English practice with short Chinese explanations when needed. Understanding and active use should guide the choice of language.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer practising one clear pronunciation model. Others prefer listening to a range of English accents. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：模仿單一口音與聽不同口音。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about pronunciation practice. Some prefer practising one clear pronunciation model, but others favour listening to a range of English accents. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, one consistent model gives beginners a clear starting point. A learner can compare the same word across several practice sessions. For example, a nursing student listens to an introduction and copies its word stress before saying a personal version. This makes a short practice task manageable.

On the other hand, English speakers do not all sound the same. Listening to different voices helps students prepare for unfamiliar speakers. A learner who only hears one recording may understand that recording well but struggle with a new one. The goal is clear communication, not an exact copy of one person.

To sum up, I support a consistent starting model and gradual exposure to other voices. Students need both a clear example and opportunities to listen flexibly.

People have different preferences about student clubs. Some prefer joining a student club, but others favour using free time mainly for individual study. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a club gives students a reason to meet people outside their usual class. Members plan an activity and practise sharing responsibilities. For example, a nursing student joins an English club and helps arrange a short conversation game. The activity gives language study a social purpose.

On the other hand, students have different amounts of free time. Someone with paid work or a long journey home may find regular meetings difficult. A compulsory club can become another attendance requirement. Some students also prefer a small informal group or an activity outside the university.

On balance, I think clubs should be easy to join but optional. Students need a choice of ways to meet people and develop interests.

People have different preferences about student paid work. Some prefer taking a small part-time job during term, but others favour keeping term-time free for study. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, paid work gives students income and experience with schedules and customers. A student may use the income for transport or course materials. For example, a short weekend shift helps with ordinary expenses and provides practice in polite conversation with people from different backgrounds.

On the other hand, work hours can compete with study, rest and placement schedules. A late change in shifts may make planning difficult. Students also have different financial needs, so a simple rule does not fit everyone. Academic support should consider the whole timetable instead of assuming that every student has equal free time.

Taking both views into account, I prefer manageable work hours and early discussion of timetable conflicts. Students who need income should receive practical support.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer creating a shared dormitory study room. Others prefer studying inside individual rooms. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.

tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about shared dormitory study space. Some prefer creating a shared dormitory study room, but others favour studying inside individual rooms. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a separate study room gives residents a place for focused work. Roommates can keep different schedules without negotiating over every activity. For example, one nursing student reviews a lecture downstairs while another rests in their shared bedroom. Clear quiet rules make the purpose of the room easy to understand.

On the other hand, a dormitory has limited space and residents need other shared facilities too. A study room may remain empty at some times and become crowded before examinations. Some students prefer a familiar desk in their own room. Access and fair use matter as much as the room itself.

To sum up, I support a shared quiet area with flexible opening hours. Residents should also agree on respectful ways to use their own rooms.

tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about weekend courses. Some prefer offering optional weekend workshops, but others favour keeping all extra lessons on weekdays. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a weekend workshop can provide a longer block of time for a focused activity. Students may be free from ordinary classes. For example, a nursing presentation workshop can include preparation, practice and feedback in one session instead of several short meetings during a crowded week.

On the other hand, weekends are also used for family visits, work and rest. Students with a long trip to campus may find an additional journey difficult. A workshop scheduled only on weekends excludes some learners. Staff also need predictable working arrangements and time to prepare the activity.

On balance, I prefer a choice of times for optional workshops. A useful course should not assume that everyone is free on the same day.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer frequent small quizzes. Others prefer one extended course project. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：小考與學期專題。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about course assessment. Some prefer frequent small quizzes, but others favour one extended course project. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, small quizzes give students regular information about their understanding. A learner notices a gap before moving to the next topic. For example, a short vocabulary quiz shows that a nursing student confuses two words, and the teacher uses a new sentence to explain the difference.

On the other hand, a project allows students to connect ideas and develop an explanation over time. A quiz may measure recognition without showing how a learner uses information. Frequent tests can also take time away from discussion and feedback. Different course goals require different forms of evidence.

Taking both views into account, I support several small checks and a meaningful project. The assessment should match the knowledge and skills taught in the course.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer hospital maps on a phone. Others prefer printed hospital visitor maps. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：紙本導覽圖與手機導覽。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about hospital visitor maps. Some prefer hospital maps on a phone, but others favour printed hospital visitor maps. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a phone map can be updated when an entrance or service desk changes. Visitors can enlarge the text and carry the map without collecting paper. For example, a family member checks the route from the main entrance to a waiting area before arriving at the hospital.

On the other hand, not every visitor has a suitable phone or enough battery power. Some people find a printed map easier to read while asking a staff member for help. A mobile page may also be difficult to use with an unfamiliar language. Directions should remain available through several routes.

To sum up, I prefer a phone map with printed copies and staff assistance as alternatives. Visitors should be able to choose a practical format.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer booking clinic appointments online. Others prefer booking appointments by telephone. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：電話預約與線上預約。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about appointment communication. Some prefer booking clinic appointments online, but others favour booking appointments by telephone. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, online booking lets a person check available times without waiting on a telephone line. A clear page can show the appointment details before confirmation. For example, a student compares several times after class and chooses one that does not conflict with a placement schedule.

On the other hand, a telephone conversation allows a person to ask about unclear arrangements. Some users need help with digital forms or do not have reliable internet access. A booking page also needs clear instructions about its limits. It should not be treated as a way to assess urgent symptoms.

On balance, I support online booking as an option with telephone assistance available. Access should not depend on digital confidence alone.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer digital information screens in waiting areas. Others prefer printed noticeboards in waiting areas. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：螢幕公告與紙本公告。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about waiting-room information. Some prefer digital information screens in waiting areas, but others favour printed noticeboards in waiting areas. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a digital screen can update information without replacing a sheet of paper. It can show a large heading and several language options. For example, a hospital uses it to explain the location of an information desk and the order of a non-clinical registration process.

On the other hand, a changing display may move to the next page before a visitor finishes reading. Printed information stays visible and does not depend on power or a working screen. Some visitors also prefer to ask a person. Important directions need to be clear at the moment someone needs them.

Taking both views into account, I prefer stable printed directions for essential locations and screens for changing notices. Both should use readable text and simple language.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer booking hospital visits in advance. Others prefer using fixed visiting periods without individual bookings. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：預約探病與固定開放時段。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about hospital visiting arrangements. Some prefer booking hospital visits in advance, but others favour using fixed visiting periods without individual bookings. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, advance bookings can help staff understand how many visitors to expect. Families can discuss a suitable time before travelling. For example, relatives with different work hours arrange one planned visit rather than arriving together without knowing the local arrangements. Clear instructions can make preparation easier.

On the other hand, a booking rule may be difficult for someone with unpredictable work or an unexpected family situation. Digital booking also creates a barrier for some visitors. Visiting arrangements need to consider the patient's wishes and the care setting. A single rule cannot explain every individual circumstance.

To sum up, I support clear visiting arrangements with a way to discuss exceptions. The patient's preferences and the unit's rules should guide the decision.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer short patient information in plain language. Others prefer longer leaflets with detailed explanations. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.

tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about information leaflet language. Some prefer short patient information in plain language, but others favour longer leaflets with detailed explanations. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, plain language makes the main message easier to follow. A clear heading and a familiar word can help a reader find the next step. For example, a visitor leaflet explains where to ask a question without using an unfamiliar department name or a long administrative phrase.

On the other hand, some information needs detail and careful explanation. Removing too much can leave a reader with unanswered questions. A short sentence is not automatically clear, especially when it contains an unexplained term. Readers also have different language and accessibility needs, so one version may not suit everyone.

On balance, I prefer a clear short summary with further detail available. Writers should check understanding rather than count sentence length alone.

tasks.prompt: Some people prefer one agreed family contact for routine updates. Others prefer separate routine updates for several relatives. Write four paragraphs about both views and give your own opinion. Include reasons and a concrete example.
tasks.zh: 主題：固定聯絡人與多人聯絡。練習比較兩種做法：開頭交代選擇，兩個主體段各寫理由及具體例子，結尾說自己的選擇。共四段，至少150字；這是意見練習，不是現行機構規定。
tasks.sample:
People have different preferences about family communication. Some prefer one agreed family contact for routine updates, but others favour separate routine updates for several relatives. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, an agreed contact can reduce repeated arrangements and help a family share general plans. For example, one relative coordinates visiting times and tells the others where to meet. Staff and families know whom to approach about practical matters, subject to the patient's permission and local rules.

On the other hand, family relationships differ, and one person may not be available or suitable for every conversation. Patients may have specific wishes about who receives information. A contact arrangement must not replace the patient's own voice. There also needs to be a way to change the arrangement when circumstances change.

Taking both views into account, I support discussing a contact arrangement with the patient rather than imposing one. Permission, privacy and flexibility are essential.

People have different preferences about student name badges. Some prefer large name badges with clear student roles, but others favour small badges with limited visible information. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the one hand, a clear role label helps people know whom they are speaking with. A visitor can distinguish a nursing student from a qualified staff member. For example, a student introduces themselves and points to the role on the badge, making the introduction easier to follow.

People have different preferences about hospital language practice. Some prefer staff English conversation groups, but others favour individual online English practice. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

A conversation group also needs a clear purpose and appropriate support. It should not replace qualified language assistance for actual patient communication.

On balance, I support optional groups alongside individual resources. Real communication needs should follow the hospital's approved language-support procedures.

People have different preferences about clinical placement travel. Some prefer placements at a wider range of locations, but others favour fewer placement locations with stable travel. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

Taking both views into account, I prefer a planned range of placements with enough time at each site. Travel and supervision need consideration before adding another location.

People have different preferences about placement orientation. Some prefer online orientation before a placement, but others favour in-person orientation on the first day. I think the decision should consider the purpose and the people involved.

On the other hand, an in-person introduction lets students see the environment and meet the team. A teacher can answer questions about current arrangements. Online information can become outdated, and some learners need help accessing it. Reading a page does not prove that a student understands local procedures.

To sum up, I support online preparation followed by an in-person orientation. Each part should have a clear purpose and a way to ask questions.

On the other hand, a live talk gives people a chance to ask questions and clarify an unfamiliar word. Some community members have limited internet access or prefer a conversation. Videos also need regular review and clear sources. Neither format should offer individual clinical advice without an appropriate assessment.

On balance, I prefer videos as one route to general information, with live opportunities for questions. The content should be accurate and easy to access.
