This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. Local information points reduce the journey needed to ask a basic question. A resident can visit a familiar place near home. For example, a community centre helps someone find the correct office for a service and explains which contact details to use.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. A central centre can bring several specialists together and offer longer opening hours. Small locations need staff, space and updated materials. A visitor may still need referral elsewhere for a detailed question. Spreading resources too thinly can make each location less useful.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. A city can examine which questions people ask most often and which journeys are difficult. It can then assign clear roles to each location. Shared, updated information prevents conflicting directions. The goal is to make the route through services understandable, not simply to increase the number of buildings.

To sum up, I support local help for common questions and central support for complex ones. Staff should know how to connect people with the right service. The advantages are most useful when the limitations are acknowledged and there is a practical alternative for people who need it.

tasks.prompt: Some people support more campus shuttle services, while others favour more parking spaces for private vehicles. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：校車與停車位。討論兩種看法並表達自己的意見。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
People have different views about campus transport. Some support more campus shuttle services, while others prefer more parking spaces for private vehicles. In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. A reliable shuttle gives students another way to reach campus without a private vehicle. Several people can share one journey. For example, a nursing student travels between a station and the school with books and a uniform without arranging a separate ride every day.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. A shuttle route cannot match every student's timetable or starting point. Early placements and late activities may require different arrangements. Parking also matters for some people with access needs. A transport plan should consider reliability and accessibility instead of assuming one option fits all journeys.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. The university can map travel times and ask students about missed connections. A trial route can show demand before a larger commitment. Clear information about the last service is essential. A cheap service is not useful if it arrives too late for class or leaves students without a way home.

To conclude, I support useful shuttle routes alongside appropriate access arrangements. The best investment depends on the journeys students actually need to make. The best choice keeps the main benefits while making room for people whose circumstances are different from the majority.

tasks.prompt: Consider a proposal favouring more bicycle parking and routes over more support for bus and walking routes. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this proposal?
tasks.zh: 主題：腳踏車設施與其他通勤支援。分析優點和缺點；題目沒有要求哪邊較多，不必硬選輸贏。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。

This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. Bicycle facilities can make a short trip more convenient for people able to cycle. Secure parking gives students a place to leave a bicycle. For example, a student rides between nearby campus buildings and avoids searching for a vehicle parking space for each short journey.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. Not everyone can cycle, and distance, weather or mobility needs can make it impractical. Pedestrians and bus passengers also need safe, accessible routes. A new bicycle rack alone does not solve a difficult junction. Transport spending needs to consider the full journey and a range of users.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. Planners can consult students and nearby residents about the routes they actually use. They can identify gaps between existing paths and destinations. Clear crossings and suitable maintenance matter after construction too. Comparing several transport options avoids presenting one mode as a complete answer to every access problem.

All things considered, I support bicycle improvements within a wider access plan. Walking, public transport and individual access needs should remain part of the decision. Its benefits are real, but they only reach everyone when the limitations are planned for in advance and explained clearly.

tasks.prompt: Some people support more electronic nursing books, while others favour more printed nursing books. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

tasks.sample:
People have different views about library collections. Some support more electronic nursing books, while others prefer more printed nursing books. In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. An electronic book can be accessed without carrying a heavy volume. Search tools help a student find a familiar term quickly. For example, a learner checks a course reading from a dormitory desk after returning from a placement, provided the library licence allows access.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. Printed books work without a charged device and offer a different reading experience. Digital licences may limit simultaneous users or require a connection. Some students find long screen reading uncomfortable. The availability of a title in digital form does not guarantee that everyone can use it easily.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. Librarians can examine borrowing requests and ask teachers which books are essential. They should compare access conditions rather than only purchase prices. Loan devices and accessible formats may help some learners. Keeping a practical route to required reading is more important than choosing one format for every title.

To sum up, I prefer a mixture based on course demand and accessibility. Students should know which format is available before an assignment deadline. Whatever the final decision is, it should be explained clearly so that people with different needs can still take part.

tasks.prompt: Consider a proposal favouring free open course materials over a required published textbook. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this proposal?
tasks.zh: 主題：開放教材與指定教科書。分析優點和缺點；題目沒有要求哪邊較多，不必硬選輸贏。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。

This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. Free materials reduce the cost of joining a course. Students can open the same reading without waiting to buy a book. For example, a teacher shares an openly available language worksheet and clearly explains the source, so everyone can prepare for the next lesson.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. A published textbook may provide a carefully organised sequence and useful teacher resources. Free material still needs review for accuracy, level and permission to reuse it. A collection of unrelated pages can be confusing. Price alone does not establish the quality of a learning resource.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. A course team can review materials before adopting them and keep a record of versions. Students need to know which sections to read and where to ask questions. Updating links and checking accessibility require time. Reducing cost is valuable, but the learning path still needs careful organisation.

To conclude, I support free materials when they meet the course goals. Teachers should explain how the readings fit together and offer clear guidance. Its advantages matter most when its limits are recognised and the people who need another option can still find one.

tasks.prompt: Some people support trying a personal revision before using a tool, while others favour using digital writing suggestions immediately. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：寫作工具與先自行修改。討論兩種看法並表達自己的意見。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
People have different views about writing assistance tools. Some support trying a personal revision before using a tool, while others prefer using digital writing suggestions immediately. In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. A personal revision encourages a learner to read the meaning and check familiar rules. The student can find a missing subject without accepting a whole rewritten paragraph. For example, a nursing student corrects a simple verb form and then explains the change to a teacher.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. Digital suggestions can draw attention to a difficulty the learner does not recognise. They may provide a useful starting question. However, a polished replacement does not show that the student understands the change. Access and the quality of suggestions also vary between tools.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. Teachers can ask learners to keep an original sentence and describe one revision. This makes the learning process visible without requiring a long technical report. Tools should support practice rather than replace the student's ideas. A later task without suggestions can show whether the learner can use the point independently.

All things considered, I prefer a first attempt and a short self-check before tool support. Students should explain accepted changes and follow course rules. Both views raise fair points, so the final arrangement should keep what works well on each side of the argument.

This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. A shared mark encourages students to take responsibility for the final result together. Members need to connect their sections and agree on a clear message. For example, a nursing group checks that its community presentation uses the same terms and does not repeat the same information.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. Contributions may differ, and one mark can hide unequal participation. A student may do careful preparation that is less visible than public speaking. Separate marks can recognise individual learning, but teachers need reliable evidence. Simply counting pages or speaking time may create another unfair measure.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. The teacher can set short progress meetings and ask each member to explain a decision. Group records should show responsibilities without becoming excessive paperwork. Students need a fair route to discuss problems early. Assessment can then reflect collaboration and individual understanding rather than only the appearance of the finished presentation.

To sum up, I prefer a shared component and a clear individual component. Students should understand both before the project begins. The approach works best when its limits are explained honestly and another reasonable option remains available to those who need it.

tasks.prompt: Some people support one deadline for the whole class, while others favour limited flexible deadlines. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. A shared deadline helps teachers organise feedback and lets the class move to the next activity together. Students know the planning target. For example, everyone submits a short essay before a feedback lesson, so the teacher can choose common problems from the same task.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. Illness, caring responsibilities and unexpected placement changes can affect available time. A rule without exceptions may assess circumstances as much as learning. Unlimited flexibility also creates confusion, so students need a clear request process. Fairness does not always mean treating different situations as identical.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. A teacher can explain the deadline, the reason for it and how to ask for help before a problem grows. Short staged tasks may prevent all work from collecting at the end. Clear communication helps both students and staff. Exceptions should follow course procedures instead of depending on who argues most strongly.

To conclude, I support normal deadlines with a transparent process for reasonable adjustments. The learning goal and the timing of feedback should guide decisions. A fair decision looks at the advantages and the costs together and offers a workable route for everyone involved.

Overall, I support normal deadlines with a transparent process for reasonable adjustments. The learning goal and the timing of feedback should guide decisions. That is why I would not turn it into a universal rule. Flexibility, rather than one requirement for everyone, gives each person a fair chance to take part.

tasks.prompt: Consider a proposal favouring a small menu of affordable campus meals over a wider menu at a higher average price. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this proposal?
tasks.zh: 主題：平價餐點與更多選項。分析優點和缺點；題目沒有要求哪邊較多，不必硬選輸贏。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。

The proposal favouring a small menu of affordable campus meals over a wider menu at a higher average price raises questions about campus meal choices. This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. Affordable meals help students plan ordinary daily spending. A predictable price is useful during a long day on campus. For example, a nursing student with a short lunch break can buy a familiar meal without travelling away from school to compare several shops.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. A limited menu may not meet different dietary preferences or access needs. Students may avoid the service if the available meals do not suit them. Variety also matters across a full week. Low prices need to be considered alongside food quality and clear information about ingredients.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. The university can ask students which options they need and publish prices clearly. A regular review can identify meals that are rarely chosen and gaps in the menu. The aim is a usable service, not simply the longest list. Decisions should include students with different budgets and needs.

All things considered, I support a few affordable core meals with some rotating choices. Students should be able to find suitable information before buying. If its weaknesses are recognised early and handled sensibly, the advantages of this approach become much easier to keep.

tasks.prompt: Some people support short study visits overseas, while others favour international learning activities at home. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. An overseas visit can expose students to a different learning environment and ordinary life in another language. A participant learns to ask practical questions in an unfamiliar place. For example, a nursing student joins an approved campus visit and compares classroom arrangements with those at home.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. Travel requires money, time and careful planning. Some students cannot leave work or family responsibilities. International guests and online exchanges can also offer useful perspectives at home. A short visit does not automatically give a full understanding of another country's professional system.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. Universities can explain the activities, supervision and expected preparation before accepting applications. Financial support may widen participation. A follow-up discussion can connect observations with course learning. The programme should avoid presenting travel itself as proof of professional competence or as a guarantee of future employment.

To sum up, I support overseas opportunities alongside accessible local alternatives. Students need clear learning goals and realistic information about costs. A useful decision weighs the benefits against the limitations and explains how people with different circumstances can take part.

tasks.prompt: Consider a proposal favouring learning about careers from alumni talks over starting with official career information. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this proposal?

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. Alumni can describe everyday experiences in a way that feels concrete. Students can ask about study habits and adapting to a new workplace. For example, a graduate explains how they organised language practice and which questions are useful before starting.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. One person's experience may not match current requirements or another student's circumstances. Formal licensing and immigration information can change. Official sources are needed for those rules. Personal stories are useful examples, but they should not become promises about a student's future route.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. To conclude, I prefer official information for requirements and alumni stories for practical perspective. Students should keep the two purposes clear. The advantages are most useful when the limitations are acknowledged and there is a practical alternative for people who need it.

tasks.prompt: Some people support protecting a dedicated staff break area, while others favour using available rooms mainly for work activities. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

People have different views about hospital staff spaces. Some support protecting a dedicated staff break area, while others prefer using available rooms mainly for work activities. In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. A separate break area gives staff somewhere to step away from active work during an authorised break. Colleagues can sit down and have a meal in an appropriate space. For example, a clearly designated room avoids using a busy corridor for ordinary break activities.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. Hospital space has many competing uses, and some departments need more rooms for essential work. A break room also needs suitable access and maintenance. An attractive room alone does not ensure that staff can take breaks. Work arrangements and local rules remain part of the discussion.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. Managers can examine how rooms are used throughout the day before making changes. Staff can describe practical difficulties with the existing arrangement. A modest, accessible room may be more useful than a large space far away. Any redesign should consider the full workflow rather than counting rooms in isolation.

All things considered, I support protected break space alongside careful planning of clinical space. The decision should include the people using both areas. The best choice keeps the main benefits while making room for people whose circumstances are different from the majority.

tasks.prompt: Consider a proposal favouring smaller clinical teaching groups over larger groups for shared explanations. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this proposal?
tasks.zh: 主題：小組帶教與大班說明。分析優點和缺點；題目沒有要求哪邊較多，不必硬選輸贏。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
The proposal favouring smaller clinical teaching groups over larger groups for shared explanations raises questions about clinical teaching groups. This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. A small group gives each student more time to ask a question and receive feedback. The teacher can notice confusion during a supervised practice. For example, several students explain an imagined communication task one at a time and discuss how to make the message clearer.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. Small groups require more teaching time and suitable space. Some general explanations can be shared effectively with a larger class. Repeating the same introduction many times may reduce time for individual follow-up. The best group size depends on the activity and available supervision.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. A course team can identify activities that need observation of each learner and protect time for those tasks. Written instructions can support general preparation. Students should know when and how to ask questions. Group size is one factor, but lesson design and useful feedback also influence the experience.

To sum up, I prefer larger sessions for common information and smaller supervised groups for practice. The teaching goal should determine the format. Its benefits are real, but they only reach everyone when the limitations are planned for in advance and explained clearly.

tasks.prompt: Some people support a regular volunteer commitment, while others favour occasional volunteer events. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：長期志工與短期活動。討論兩種看法並表達自己的意見。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
People have different views about volunteer programmes. Some support a regular volunteer commitment, while others prefer occasional volunteer events. In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. Regular volunteering can help a student understand a community organisation over time. The learner becomes familiar with the agreed role and schedule. For example, a student helps at a non-clinical information event each month and gradually learns how the team organises its materials.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. A long commitment may not fit changing course and placement schedules. Occasional events allow more people to take part. Volunteers also need training and a role within their abilities. Attendance alone is not a reason to ask a student to perform tasks outside that role.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. An organisation can describe the task, time commitment and supervision before recruiting. Students can discuss changes in availability early. A short review after an event helps identify useful learning and practical issues. Programmes should value reliable, appropriate participation rather than simply the largest number of recorded hours.

To conclude, I support both regular and occasional volunteering with clear responsibilities. Participation should fit the student's timetable and the organisation's needs. Whatever the final decision is, it should be explained clearly so that people with different needs can still take part.

tasks.prompt: Consider a proposal favouring reading research articles in a guided group over starting with short research summaries. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this proposal?
tasks.zh: 主題：研究讀書會與短篇摘要。分析優點和缺點；題目沒有要求哪邊較多，不必硬選輸贏。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
The proposal favouring reading research articles in a guided group over starting with short research summaries raises questions about student research access. This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. A guided group can show students how a research article is organised. Learners ask where a claim comes from and how the study was described. For example, a teacher helps the group locate the research question and separate the authors' findings from their wider discussion.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. A full article can contain unfamiliar methods and difficult vocabulary. Beginners may spend all their time translating without understanding the purpose. A clear summary can provide a starting point, but it may leave out limitations. The difficulty needs to fit the teaching support available.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. Teachers can choose a narrow reading question instead of asking students to understand every sentence at once. The class can compare a summary with the original section and identify omitted detail. This builds a habit of checking evidence. Reading length alone does not show how carefully a student has understood a claim.

All things considered, I prefer accessible summaries followed by selected parts of full articles. Students can gradually take on more detailed reading with guidance. Its advantages matter most when its limits are recognised and the people who need another option can still find one.

For example, a community centre offers a general service-information session after dinner and leaves time for visitors to ask practical questions.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. Evenings do not suit everyone. Some people work at night, care for family members or have limited transport after dark. Staff and venues also have opening restrictions. Daytime sessions can be more convenient for other groups. One time slot cannot represent the whole community.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. A small survey can identify likely participants and the barriers they face. Repeating a session at another time may reach more people than making one event larger. Materials should also explain where to ask a later question. Planning should focus on who can participate, not only on how many seats are available.

To sum up, I prefer a varied schedule and clear information in more than one format. Organisers should ask the intended audience about access. Both views raise fair points, so the final arrangement should keep what works well on each side of the argument.

Making it compulsory for everyone would solve one problem but create several others. The aim should be an arrangement that works in practice for different people.

tasks.prompt: Consider a proposal favouring more quiet outdoor spaces on campus over more indoor teaching rooms. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this proposal?
tasks.zh: 主題：綠地與新教室。分析優點和缺點；題目沒有要求哪邊較多，不必硬選輸贏。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
The proposal favouring more quiet outdoor spaces on campus over more indoor teaching rooms raises questions about campus environment. This approach offers practical advantages, but it also has limitations. Both sides need consideration because an arrangement that works well for one person may be less suitable for another.

One important advantage concerns the way people can carry out the activity. Outdoor spaces give students a place for informal conversation or a short break between activities. A shaded seating area can also support small non-clinical group discussions. For example, students review an English dialogue together outside before returning to the library for individual work.

There are also disadvantages that the proposal should address. Teaching rooms are necessary for scheduled classes and suitable equipment. A growing course may struggle to find space at busy times. Weather also limits the use of outdoor areas. The value of a green space needs consideration alongside the practical requirements of the learning programme.

These disadvantages do not mean that the proposal has no value, but they affect how it should be organised. The university can examine room bookings across the week and improve scheduling before removing outdoor space. Students and teachers can identify which spaces are actually useful. A plan can combine accessible indoor rooms with places for informal activity. The decision should consider long-term use, not just a single crowded day.

To conclude, I support protecting useful outdoor areas while reviewing how existing classrooms are used. New construction should answer a clear need. The approach works best when its limits are explained honestly and another reasonable option remains available to those who need it.

tasks.prompt: Institutions promote more quiet outdoor spaces on campus, but some people find this approach difficult to use or fit into their routine. What problems can this cause, and what solutions can you suggest?
tasks.zh: 主題：綠地與新教室。問題與解決題：每個方法都要對應前面提出的困難。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
When institutions promote more quiet outdoor spaces on campus, the change can cause practical difficulties for some people. A new approach may be useful, but people differ in their access, experience and available time. This essay considers the problems and suggests ways to make the arrangement more workable.

The main problems become clear when the proposal meets different individual circumstances. Teaching rooms are necessary for scheduled classes and suitable equipment. A growing course may struggle to find space at busy times. Weather also limits the use of outdoor areas. The value of a green space needs consideration alongside the practical requirements of the learning programme. A person who cannot use the main arrangement may then miss a useful opportunity or need extra help to take part.

One solution is to improve the design and explain the available support clearly. The university can examine room bookings across the week and improve scheduling before removing outdoor space. Students and teachers can identify which spaces are actually useful. A plan can combine accessible indoor rooms with places for informal activity. The decision should consider long-term use, not just a single crowded day.

Another solution is to retain an appropriate alternative instead of assuming the main approach suits everyone. I support protecting useful outdoor areas while reviewing how existing classrooms are used. New construction should answer a clear need. This still allows the useful features of the proposal to remain. Outdoor spaces give students a place for informal conversation or a short break between activities.

In conclusion, quiet outdoor spaces give students a place to rest and talk, but teaching rooms are still necessary and the weather limits outdoor use. Reviewing how existing rooms are booked and protecting the outdoor areas that people actually use would balance both needs.

tasks.prompt: Some people support sharing study notes with classmates, while others favour keeping individual notes until personal review is complete. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
tasks.zh: 主題：共用筆記與個人筆記。討論兩種看法並表達自己的意見。至少250字，提出解釋與具體例子；範文是練習示範，不代表保證取得某個雅思級分。
tasks.sample:
People have different views about shared learning resources. Some support sharing study notes with classmates, while others prefer keeping individual notes until personal review is complete. In my opinion, the choice should depend on the purpose and the needs of the people involved. Neither option needs to become the only acceptable approach in every situation.

Supporters of the first option have several reasons for their view. Shared notes can help classmates notice a missing point or compare explanations. A learner can ask why another person organised a topic differently. For example, two nursing students compare an outline after class and check an uncertain detail against the approved course material.

However, the alternative also deserves attention. Personal notes may contain mistakes or shorthand that another person misunderstands. Copying a complete set can also replace the work of thinking through the lesson. Students need to respect course rules and avoid sharing confidential material. A large folder of notes is not automatically a reliable learning resource.

A practical response should connect these arguments with the way the service or course actually works. A study group can agree to label uncertain points and check them with the teacher. It can share a short explanation of an idea instead of uploading every private note. This makes responsibility clearer. The aim is to support understanding while preserving each learner's active role in the study process.

All things considered, I prefer voluntary sharing after personal review, with sources clearly identified. Classmates should discuss questions rather than simply copy one another's pages. A fair decision looks at the advantages and the costs together and offers a workable route for everyone involved.

grammar.title: Task 2：先認題型，再選開頭和論點
points: 討論兩方（Discuss both views）：開頭交代兩種看法並表態；主體段兩邊都要討論，不能只寫自己支持的那一邊。
問題＋解決（Problems and solutions）：開頭說明問題範圍；每個解法都要對應前面提出的問題，這類題目不一定要寫同不同意。
優點＋缺點（Advantages and disadvantages）：開頭點出要比較的兩面；題目若問哪邊較多，還要明確回答。
同意程度（To what extent）：用 I agree／I partly agree／I disagree 說清楚程度；兩個主體段支持這個立場，結論保持一致。

examples.en: Some people support free hospital care, while others think patients should pay.
examples.zh: 有人支持免費醫療，也有人認為病人應付費。（討論兩方；while 在這裡表示對照。）

examples.en: This essay discusses the problems and suggests solutions.
examples.zh: 本文討論問題並提出解決方法。（問題＋解決的開頭。）

examples.en: Online learning has both advantages and disadvantages.
examples.zh: 線上學習有優點，也有缺點。（優缺點題的開頭。）

examples.en: I partly agree that more sports facilities improve public health.
examples.zh: 我部分同意增加運動設施能改善大眾健康。（說清楚同意的程度。）

mistakes.bad: I am partly agree with this view.
mistakes.good: I partly agree with this view.
mistakes.why: agree 是動詞，前面不加 am；partly 表示部分同意。

mistakes.bad: In conclusion, a completely different issue is important too.
mistakes.good: In conclusion, both views have value, but I support the first for these reasons.
mistakes.why: 結論要收回前面已經說明的論點，不突然換一個沒討論的議題。

stages.name: ⑭ 橋接段落
stages.goal: 用這一課的文法寫一段，句子之間接得順
criteria: 用到這一課的文法，而且用對
內容回答了題目每一點
句子之間接得順（時間、因果、轉折）
文法和用字正確

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 100 words) about a time something unexpected happened to you at school, at work or on a trip. Use the past simple, the past continuous and the past perfect.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 100 字）：一次在學校、打工或旅行時發生的意外事件。要用到過去式、過去進行式和過去完成式。
tasks.sample: Last winter, something unexpected happened on my way to school. I was waiting for the bus in the rain when an old man near me suddenly fell down. At first, nobody moved, because everyone was looking at their phones. I had learned basic first aid in class the week before, so I knelt next to him and asked if he was hurt. He told me that he had not eaten anything since the night before and felt dizzy. I gave him my sandwich and asked another student to call an ambulance. By the time the ambulance arrived, he was feeling better. I missed my first class that day, but I did not mind at all.
tasks.focus: 敘事時態：過去式、過去進行式、過去完成式、used to

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 120 words) comparing your life now with your life when you were a child. Use "used to" for things that are no longer true, and the past simple for one special memory.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 120 字）：比較你現在和小時候的生活。已經不再這樣的習慣用 used to，再用過去式講一個特別的回憶。
tasks.sample: When I was a child, my life was very different from my life now. I used to live with my grandparents in a small town in Chiayi. I used to wake up early because my grandfather took me to the market every morning. I also used to be afraid of doctors and hospitals, and I cried every time I had an injection. Now I live in a busy city, I usually sleep late, and I am studying to become a nurse. One memory is still very clear. When I was eight, my grandmother was in hospital for a week. A kind nurse let me help her check my grandmother's temperature. I had never felt so useful before. Maybe that was the day I first wanted to be a nurse.
tasks.focus: 敘事時態：過去式、過去進行式、過去完成式、used to

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 100 words) about your plans for next weekend. Include an arrangement you have made (present continuous), what you will be doing at a certain time (will be + -ing), and something you will have finished by Sunday night (will have + past participle).
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 100 字）：下個週末的計畫。要有已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、某個時間你會正在做的事（will be + -ing），以及星期天晚上以前會完成的事（will have + 過去分詞）。
tasks.sample: I have a busy weekend ahead. On Saturday morning, I'm meeting my classmates at the library, because we have a pharmacology test next week. At ten o'clock, we will be going through the chapter on antibiotics together. In the afternoon, I'm visiting my grandmother, who lives near the station. This time on Saturday evening, I will probably be helping her cook dinner. On Sunday, I'm going to sleep late and then do some shopping. By Sunday night, I will have finished my notes for the test, and I will have cleaned my room. I hope I will also have time to watch a movie.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 120 words) about where you see yourself in five years. Use "will be + -ing" and "will have + past participle", and give reasons.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 120 字）：五年後的你會在哪裡、在做什麼？用 will be + -ing 和 will have + 過去分詞，並說明理由。
tasks.sample: In five years, I hope my life will look very different. By then, I will have graduated from university, and I will have passed the nursing licensing exam. I will probably be working in a large hospital in Taipei, because I want to gain experience in an intensive care unit. I will also be preparing for the IELTS test, since my dream is to work as a nurse in the United States. By the time I am twenty-six, I will have saved enough money to take the exam and apply for a visa. I know that it will not be easy at all. However, if I keep studying a little every day, I believe I will be ready when the chance comes.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Look at the clues and write a paragraph (about 100 words). Your roommate's bed hasn't been slept in, her umbrella is wet, there are two concert tickets on the table, and her phone is switched off. What must, might or can't have happened? Explain each guess with a clue.
tasks.zh: 看線索寫一段（約 100 字）：室友的床沒有睡過的痕跡、她的雨傘是濕的、桌上有兩張演唱會門票、她的手機關機。用 must／might／can't (have) 推測發生了什麼，每個推測都要說是根據哪個線索。
tasks.sample: My roommate can't have stayed at home last night, because her bed hasn't been slept in. Her umbrella is wet, so she must have been outside in the rain at some point. The two concert tickets on the table are another clue. She might have planned to go to a concert with a friend, but the tickets are still here, so perhaps the concert is on another day. Her phone is switched off, so the battery might have died, or she might have turned it off herself. These clues don't tell me where she slept. She might have stayed at a friend's place, but I can't be sure, so I will send her a message and wait for her reply.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 120 words) about a time you had to guess what was wrong with someone, such as a friend, a family member or a patient. What clues did you notice, and what did you think must, might or can't have happened?
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 120 字）：有一次你必須猜朋友、家人或病人怎麼了。你注意到哪些線索？你推測一定、可能、不可能發生了什麼？
tasks.sample: Last month, my younger brother came home from school and went straight to his room without saying hello. This was strange, because he usually talks non-stop about his day. At first, I thought he must be tired, since he had a basketball game that afternoon. Then I noticed that his school bag was much lighter than usual. He might have left his books at school, or someone might have taken them. When I knocked on his door, I saw that his eyes were red. He can't have been only tired; something must have upset him. In the end, he told me that he had lost his new phone and was afraid our parents would be angry. We looked for it together and found it in his basketball shoes.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 100 words) about a time something went wrong because of a small decision. Describe what happened, then write at least three sentences with "If I had…, I would/wouldn't have…".
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 100 字）：一個小決定讓事情出錯的經驗。先說發生了什麼，再寫至少三句 If I had…, I would/wouldn't have…。
tasks.sample: Last semester, I made a small decision that caused a big problem. The night before my anatomy exam, I decided to watch just one episode of a drama. One episode became four, and I went to bed at three in the morning. The next day, I overslept and arrived at the exam twenty minutes late. If I had turned off my computer after one episode, I wouldn't have stayed up so late. If I had set two alarms, I would have woken up on time. If I had arrived earlier, I could have finished all the questions. I passed the exam, but only just. Now I never start a drama before an exam.
tasks.focus: 第三類假設：If + had + 過去分詞，would／could／might have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 120 words) about an important event in history or in your family. How would things have been different if it hadn't happened? Use the third conditional at least three times.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 120 字）：歷史上或你家裡的一件重要事件。如果它當初沒有發生，事情會有什麼不同？至少用三次第三類假設。
tasks.sample: An important event in my family happened in 1999, when my grandparents moved from a small village in Yunlin to Taichung. My grandfather had found a job in a factory there. If they hadn't moved, my father wouldn't have gone to a good high school in the city, and he might not have become an engineer. He also met my mother in Taichung, so if my grandparents had stayed in the village, my parents would probably never have met. Of course, the move was hard for my grandmother. She missed her friends, and she often says that if she had known how lonely she would feel, she might have refused to go. Still, I am grateful that they took the risk.
tasks.focus: 第三類假設：If + had + 過去分詞，would／could／might have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 100 words) about two things you wish were different in your life now, and why. Then write about one thing you wish you had done differently in the past.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 100 字）：你希望現在生活中哪兩件事不一樣、為什麼（wish + 過去式）；再寫一件你希望過去做得不一樣的事（wish + had + 過去分詞）。
tasks.sample: There are two things I wish were different in my life right now. First, I wish I had more free time. Between classes, homework and my part-time job, I hardly have time to see my friends. Second, I wish my English were better, because I want to work abroad one day and I still feel nervous when I speak. I also have one regret about the past. When I was in high school, I spent most evenings playing games. I wish I had used that time to read English books or practise speaking. If only I could go back and tell my younger self to start earlier!
tasks.focus: 願望和遺憾：wish／if only + 過去式（現在）、wish／if only + had + 過去分詞（過去）、should／shouldn't have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 120 words) giving advice to a first-year nursing student, based on your own mistakes. Use "should have" / "shouldn't have" for your mistakes and "should" for your advice.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 120 字）：用你自己犯過的錯給大一護理系學生建議。說自己的錯用 should have／shouldn't have，給建議用 should。
tasks.sample: If I could give one piece of advice to a first-year nursing student, it would be this: take care of yourself as well as your patients. In my first year, I made a few mistakes. I shouldn't have stayed up so late before early classes, because I was always tired and couldn't concentrate. I should have joined a study group, too. I tried to learn everything alone, and when I didn't understand something, I just gave up. I also should have asked my teachers more questions instead of worrying about what others thought. So, my advice is simple. You should sleep enough, find classmates to study with, and never be afraid to ask. These small habits will make the next four years much easier.
tasks.focus: 願望和遺憾：wish／if only + 過去式（現在）、wish／if only + had + 過去分詞（過去）、should／shouldn't have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 100 words) introducing three people in your life. Use non-defining relative clauses with who, whose and where, and remember the commas.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 100 字）：介紹你生活中的三個人。用加逗號的 who、whose、where 補充說明。
tasks.sample: I would like to introduce three important people in my life. The first is my mother, who works as an accountant in Kaohsiung. She is the most patient person I know. The second is my best friend, Jenny, whose family runs a small noodle shop near our old school. We have been friends since we were seven, and I still visit the shop every summer. The third is my high school biology teacher, Mr. Chen, who made me interested in the human body. He now teaches in Pingtung, where he grew up. Without these three people, I would not be studying nursing today.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph (about 120 words) describing a place you know well, such as your school, your hometown or a hospital. Use at least four non-defining relative clauses with who, which, whose or where, and remember the commas.
tasks.zh: 寫一段（約 120 字）：介紹一個你很熟的地方（學校、家鄉或醫院）。至少用四個加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明。
tasks.sample: I would like to describe my nursing school, which is on a hill just outside Taichung. The main building, which was built in the 1970s, is old but full of character. On the first floor is the skills lab, where we practise giving injections on plastic arms. Our favourite teacher, Ms. Wang, who worked in an intensive care unit for fifteen years, teaches most of our lab classes. Next to the lab is the library, whose big windows look out over the city. In the evenings, many students study there until it closes at ten. Behind the school there is a small night market, where we often eat after class. I will miss this place when I graduate, which will be in two years.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph about a missed campus shuttle. Explain what was happening, what had happened earlier, and what you did next. Include one old habit with used to.
tasks.zh: 單元48加練：錯過校園接駁車。用過去進行式寫當時正在做什麼、過去完成式寫更早發生的事，再用過去式交代結果；加一句 used to 舊習慣。至少100字。
tasks.sample: Last Monday, I missed the campus shuttle before an English workshop. I was checking my bag when the bus left the stop. I had read the old timetable instead of the new one. I used to leave my room at the last possible minute, so I had no spare time that morning. I called the course office and explained the delay. Then I checked the next service and waited at the correct stop. I arrived during the first break and asked the teacher which activity I had missed. Looking back, the event showed me one practical weakness in my preparation. I changed a small habit afterwards, so the same situation became easier to manage.
tasks.focus: 敘事時態：過去式、過去進行式、過去完成式、used to

tasks.prompt: Write about a missed campus shuttle. Briefly explain the mistake, then use at least three third conditional sentences to imagine different past decisions and results. End with a practical lesson.
tasks.zh: 單元51加練：錯過校園接駁車。先說實際發生的事，再至少寫三句 If＋had＋過去分詞，would／could／might have＋過去分詞，最後說現在學到什麼。至少120字。
tasks.sample: Last Monday, I missed the campus shuttle before an English workshop. I was checking my bag when the bus left the stop. I had read the old timetable instead of the new one. If I had checked the current timetable, I would have known the earlier departure time. If I had left my room sooner, I could have caught the shuttle. If I had packed my bag the night before, I would not have needed another check at the stop. The result was inconvenient, but it gave me a useful chance to review my preparation. I should check the latest timetable before an unfamiliar journey. I should also prepare my bag in advance and leave time for an unexpected delay.
tasks.focus: 第三類假設：If + had + 過去分詞，would／could／might have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write a reflection on a missed campus shuttle. Include two present wishes, one past wish, one sentence with should have, one with should not have, and practical advice for next time.
tasks.zh: 單元52加練：錯過校園接駁車。兩個現在願望用 wish＋過去式，一個過去遺憾用 wish＋had＋過去分詞；各加一句 should have、should not have，最後提出下一次的做法。至少120字。
tasks.sample: Last Monday, I missed the campus shuttle before an English workshop. The experience made me think about both my present habits and my earlier choices. I wish I were more careful with travel information. I wish I had a little more time before morning classes. I wish I had checked the new timetable on Sunday. I should have packed my bag earlier. I should not have relied on an old screenshot. I cannot change that day, but I can make a practical adjustment now. I should check the latest timetable before an unfamiliar journey. I should also prepare my bag in advance and leave time for an unexpected delay. My aim is to prepare more clearly next time, not to keep blaming myself for a mistake that already happened.
tasks.focus: 願望和遺憾：wish／if only + 過去式（現在）、wish／if only + had + 過去分詞（過去）、should／shouldn't have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write a paragraph about a changed classroom. Explain what was happening, what had happened earlier, and what you did next. Include one old habit with used to.
tasks.zh: 單元48加練：教室臨時更換。用過去進行式寫當時正在做什麼、過去完成式寫更早發生的事，再用過去式交代結果；加一句 used to 舊習慣。至少100字。
tasks.sample: Last week, I went to the wrong room for a nursing presentation. I was arranging my notes on an empty desk when a cleaner asked about my class. The teacher had moved the session to another building and had posted a notice online. I used to check only the printed timetable, so I had missed the update. I looked at the course page and walked to the new room. My group had not started its presentation yet. I explained the mistake quietly and joined them before our turn. Looking back, the event showed me one practical weakness in my preparation. I changed a small habit afterwards, so the same situation became easier to manage.
tasks.focus: 敘事時態：過去式、過去進行式、過去完成式、used to

tasks.prompt: Write about a changed classroom. Briefly explain the mistake, then use at least three third conditional sentences to imagine different past decisions and results. End with a practical lesson.
tasks.zh: 單元51加練：教室臨時更換。先說實際發生的事，再至少寫三句 If＋had＋過去分詞，would／could／might have＋過去分詞，最後說現在學到什麼。至少120字。
tasks.sample: Last week, I went to the wrong room for a nursing presentation. I was arranging my notes on an empty desk when a cleaner asked about my class. The teacher had moved the session to another building and had posted a notice online. If I had checked the course page, I would have seen the room change. If I had arrived earlier, I could have found the new room without rushing. If I had contacted my group, they would have told me where to go. The result was inconvenient, but it gave me a useful chance to review my preparation. I should check official course notices before an important activity. I should save the contact details for my group and allow time to find an unfamiliar room.
tasks.focus: 第三類假設：If + had + 過去分詞，would／could／might have + 過去分詞
