That evening, I am meeting my project partner to discuss the list. By Friday, we will have selected the readings for our outline. We will check relevance and reliability rather than choose a source only because it appears first.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a new dormitory arrangement. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：宿舍重新安排。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My roommate and I are reorganising our room on Sunday afternoon. We agreed on the plan yesterday because our desks have become crowded with course materials. At two o'clock, I will be sorting my English and nursing folders while my roommate clears a shared shelf. By four, we will have decided where our common items belong. I will also have separated current coursework from older practice pages. We are keeping each person's private belongings separate and asking before moving them. At seven o'clock that evening, we will be checking whether the new arrangement leaves enough room for both desks. By bedtime, I will have prepared my bag for Monday. We hope the changes make ordinary study easier, but we can adjust the arrangement after trying it for a week.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a conversation club meeting. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：英語口說社聚會。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: I am leading one short activity at our English conversation club this Friday. The club organiser has approved the topic and given me ten minutes. At six thirty, I will be explaining a simple game about asking for directions on campus. At six thirty-five, the members will be practising in pairs with an imaginary map. By the end of my section, everyone will have had a chance to ask and answer a question. I will also have collected general comments about the instructions. I am rehearsing the introduction with a friend on Thursday. By Friday afternoon, I will have prepared the cards and checked the room booking. My aim is clear participation, so I will keep the task simple and leave time for questions.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a planned study break. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：安排好的讀書休息。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: I am taking a planned break with a classmate after our final lesson on Thursday. We agreed to meet at a nearby café for a short conversation. Before that, I will be finishing the outline for my English paragraph in the library. By five o'clock, I will have saved the outline and written down the next step. At five thirty, we will be talking about our week instead of checking assignments the whole time. At eight o'clock that evening, I will be preparing my materials for the next day. By bedtime, I will have packed my bag and checked Friday's timetable. I am leaving the rest of the evening free. This plan gives each activity a place without making the break depend on finishing every possible piece of work.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a student mentor meeting. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：學長姐陪伴活動。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: I am meeting my student mentor next Tuesday after class. We arranged the time because I have several practical questions about campus resources. At four o'clock, we will be looking at the library booking page together. At four thirty, we will be discussing ways to organise an ordinary study week. By the end of the meeting, I will have identified the correct staff contact for questions about formal course requirements. I will also have made a short list of resources to try. My mentor is sharing personal experience, so I will check official rules with the school. By the following Tuesday, I will have tried one useful suggestion and noted whether it fits my timetable. I am bringing my planner to make the conversation specific.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a student careers fair. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：學生職涯博覽會。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: I am attending the university careers fair with two classmates next month. We have checked the event date and chosen several talks about nursing work and further study. At ten o'clock, we will be listening to a session about preparing questions for employers. At eleven o'clock, we will be visiting the public information stands. By the end of the day, I will have collected general contact details and identified the official sources I need to check. I will not treat a short conversation as a guarantee of employment or licensing eligibility. By the following weekend, I will have organised my notes and selected two questions for the careers adviser. We are planning a break between talks so that we have time to discuss the information carefully.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a small group reading discussion. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：小組閱讀討論。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our reading group is meeting in the library next Thursday morning. The teacher has selected a short article and given us three questions to guide the discussion. At ten o'clock, we will be comparing our answers to the first question. At ten thirty, we will be identifying the parts of the text that support our explanations. By the end of the meeting, we will have agreed on a short summary and a list of points to check with the teacher. I will also have marked the words I need to review. We are reading the article separately before we meet. By Wednesday evening, I will have written an initial answer for each question, so I can contribute my own ideas instead of waiting for someone else's answer.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a practice interview. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：模擬面談。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: I am taking part in a practice interview at the careers office next Friday. An adviser has confirmed the appointment and explained that it is a learning activity. At eleven o'clock, I will be answering questions about my study interests and a group project. At eleven thirty, the adviser will be discussing my answers with me. By the end of the appointment, I will have identified one point about organisation and one point about clear speech to improve. I will also have asked how to prepare a better example. On Thursday evening, I am rehearsing with a classmate. By then, I will have prepared a short outline of my experience. I want to explain real learning honestly rather than memorise claims that do not describe me.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Write about your plan for a course project submission. Include an arranged activity with the present continuous, what will be happening at two specific times, and what will have been completed by a deadline. Explain one reason for the plan.
tasks.zh: 單元49加練：課程專題繳交。已約好的活動用現在進行式；兩個未來時間點正在做的事用 will be＋-ing；期限前完成的事用 will have＋過去分詞。再說一個安排理由，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our group is submitting a course project next Monday. We have agreed on the main file and assigned the final checks. At three o'clock on Sunday afternoon, I will be reading the introduction and checking whether it matches the assignment question. At five o'clock, my partner will be checking the source list. By Sunday evening, we will have corrected the agreed changes and saved the final version. We are meeting online for a short confirmation before the deadline. By Monday morning, the designated group member will have submitted the file through the official course page. Everyone will check the confirmation afterwards. We are leaving time for a technical problem instead of planning to upload at the final minute, and we will contact the teacher through the normal process if needed.
tasks.focus: 未來的說法：已經約好的安排（現在進行式）、will be + -ing、will have + 過去分詞

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a room reservation: Your confirmation shows Friday the 12th, but today is Friday the 5th. The room is reserved by another group today. Your classmate says she selected the first Friday she saw on the calendar. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：自習室預約線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our confirmation must be for next week, because it clearly shows Friday the twelfth and today is the fifth. We cannot treat it as a reservation for today. My classmate might have selected the wrong week when she used the booking calendar. She said she chose the first Friday she saw, but I do not know exactly what appeared on her screen. The other group must have a reservation for today, because the room is confirmed as reserved for that group. Our confirmation cannot have guaranteed this room for the fifth, since it gives a different date. I should check our account and ask library staff about an available space. A possible explanation is useful, but it is not the same as a confirmed fact about my classmate's actions.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a returned library book: Your account marks a textbook as returned at 10 a.m. Your classmate confirms she returned it for you. The book is no longer in your bag, and the library says it is being processed. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：圖書館還書線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My classmate must have returned the textbook, because she confirmed the action and the library account records it at ten o'clock. The empty space in my bag fits that explanation, but the account record is stronger evidence. The book might still be near the returns desk while staff process it. I cannot know its exact shelf location from the account alone. It cannot have remained in my bag all morning, because the library has confirmed receipt. My classmate might have used a self-service machine, but I should ask her before describing that detail as a fact. If I need the book again, I should check the library's current availability rather than assume it is ready to borrow. These clues support a return, not every detail of the return process.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about an online lesson recording: The course page says yesterday's lesson was recorded. The teacher confirms the upload is unfinished. A classmate cannot find a video link and guesses the lesson was cancelled. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：線上課程錄影線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The missing link cannot be proof that the lesson was cancelled. The course page says the lesson was recorded, and the teacher has confirmed an unfinished upload. The recording must exist in some form, although I do not know whether the final file is ready. The upload might have taken longer than expected, or the teacher might have needed more time to check it. Those are possibilities, not confirmed reasons. My classmate cannot have checked the finished video on this page yet, because the teacher says the upload is not complete. I should look for the teacher's next update and ask about the expected access time if necessary. A missing item on a website does not justify inventing a whole story about what happened during the class.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a changed workshop room: The latest official notice gives Room 204. Your printed timetable gives Room 102. The teacher confirms that the workshop moved yesterday, but gives no reason for the change. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：工作坊教室更換線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The workshop must be in Room 204 according to the current official notice and the teacher's confirmation. My printed timetable must be out of date. The change might have happened because another activity needed the old room, but the teacher has not explained the reason. A problem with equipment is another possibility, so I should not present either guess as a fact. The printed timetable cannot have been updated with yesterday's change, because it still shows Room 102. I should tell my group the confirmed room number and direct them to the latest notice. If someone needs an accessible route, we can ask the course office for help. We have enough information to find the workshop even though we do not know why the location changed.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a presentation backup: Two files are named draft and final. The final file has today's agreed changes. Your group leader confirms that final is the approved version, but nobody knows why draft was attached to an earlier message. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：簡報備份線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The file named final must be the version our group should use, because it contains the agreed changes and the group leader has confirmed it. The draft cannot be the approved final version, because our group leader clearly approved the file named final. Someone might have attached it by mistake, or the message might have been written before the changes were complete. We do not have enough evidence to blame a particular person. The group must have completed a revision, because the new file includes the changes we discussed today. I should check the file before submitting it and ask the group to use one clearly named copy. It is better to resolve the version problem than to describe an uncertain guess about the earlier message as a fact.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a delayed campus bus: The live service notice confirms a ten-minute delay. The scheduled departure time has passed. A classmate says the road looks wet, but the operator has not stated the cause. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：接駁車延誤線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The campus bus must be delayed, because the operator's current notice confirms a ten-minute delay. It cannot be described as running exactly on schedule at this moment. The wet road might have affected the journey, but that is only a possible explanation. The driver might also have faced another delay that we cannot see from the stop. We should not claim that rain caused the problem without confirmation. The operator must have posted an update, because the notice is visible, but it does not explain the underlying cause. I should check for further updates and tell my teacher if the delay affects my arrival. The notice gives useful information about timing, but it does not establish every cause of the late service.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a study partner's short message: Your partner writes, "I am at the dentist. I will reply after the appointment." You receive no further message for half an hour. You do not know when the appointment will end. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：語伴簡短訊息的線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My partner might still be unavailable for our conversation, because the last message mentioned a dental appointment and I do not know when it will finish. The lack of another reply cannot prove that my partner is angry with me. The appointment might have lasted longer than expected, or the phone might be inside a bag. I do not know which explanation is correct. My partner must have intended to reply later, because that intention appears in the message, but the exact time is uncertain. I should send one clear note about rearranging our practice and wait for a response. I should not infer a medical problem from the delay. The available evidence tells me about an appointment and a plan to reply, not about the person's feelings or health.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about an unfinished group document: The shared document contains headings but no body paragraphs. A group member confirms that the outline is complete and the writing will start tomorrow. Another member thinks the text was deleted. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：小組文件尚未完成。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The document must currently be an outline, because it contains headings and the group member has confirmed that stage of work. The missing paragraphs cannot prove that someone deleted a complete report. The group might have spent more time on planning, or the group might have planned to start writing tomorrow. I should check the agreed task list instead of assuming a mistake. The group member cannot have meant that the full report was finished, since the message explicitly says the writing has not started. I should confirm which section I need to draft and when the group will review it. This gives us a practical next step. The difference between an unfinished task and a lost task matters, so the explanation needs evidence.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about an event registration: You have an email saying your registration is confirmed. The event website still shows an old waiting-list notice. The organiser replies that your place is secure and the public page has not yet been updated. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：活動報名線索。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My place at the event must be confirmed, because both the email and the organiser's reply say so. The old public notice cannot cancel that individual confirmation by itself. The website might be waiting for an update, and the organiser has specifically said it is not current. Someone might have been busy with other event arrangements, but I do not know the reason for the delay. The organiser must have sent a reply, because the message is in my account. I can ask for the booking details if anything remains unclear. I should keep the email and follow the arrival instructions. I should not tell other people that places are available, because my own confirmed place does not show the status of everyone else's application.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a missing personal notebook: You remember using a notebook in the library. The library confirms it has found a notebook matching your description. You have not yet checked it in person, and nobody saw how it was left behind. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：找不到個人筆記本。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The notebook at the library might be mine, because its description matches the one I used there. However, a matching colour and cover do not prove ownership. I might have left it on a desk, or it might have fallen from my bag nearby. Nobody has confirmed how it was found, so I cannot choose one explanation as a fact. The library must have found some notebook, because staff have told me directly. I cannot have verified that it is mine yet, since I have not checked it. I should follow the library's collection process and confirm suitable identifying details. I should also avoid putting patient information in a personal study notebook. The first task is to verify the item, not to invent a story about losing it.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a cancelled practice room booking: The booking system records your cancellation yesterday. You remember pressing cancel and received a cancellation email. Today the room is booked by someone else, but you do not know when they reserved it. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：練習室取消預約。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My earlier booking must have been cancelled, because I remember the action and have a matching email. The system record provides another confirmation. I cannot still claim that reservation for today. The other person might have booked the room after my cancellation, or they might have used a different reservation arrangement. I do not know the timing, so I should not make an accusation about taking my place. I must have received enough information to notice the cancellation, because the email is in my account. If I cancelled by mistake, I should check current availability and ask staff about the proper next step. The evidence supports one clear action in my account, but it does not reveal every action taken by another user.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about an incomplete course upload: The course page says your file is still a draft. You saved the file but did not press the final submit button. The teacher confirms no submission has arrived, and the deadline is tomorrow. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：課程作業上傳未完成。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My file must still be a draft, because the course page says so and I did not press the final submit button. It cannot have reached the teacher as a completed submission, since the teacher has confirmed that none has arrived. I might have assumed that saving and submitting meant the same thing. That explanation fits my actions, but I should check the instructions carefully now. The deadline must still be ahead of me, because the current course notice gives tomorrow's date. I should open the saved file, confirm that it is the correct version and complete the normal submission process. Then I should check the confirmation. The important distinction is between keeping my work on the page and actually sending it for assessment.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a classmate's changed timetable: Your classmate sends a new timetable showing a laboratory class on Thursday. The old timetable showed Wednesday. The school confirms a change but has not said whether every group changed. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：同學的課表改動。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My classmate's laboratory class must now be on Thursday, because the new timetable and the school's confirmation agree. The old Wednesday entry cannot be treated as current for that group. Other groups might have changed too, but we do not have information about them. Some groups might still follow their original schedule. My classmate must have received an updated timetable, since the new document shows the confirmed change. I should check my own official timetable before changing my plans. I should not copy another group's schedule simply because we study the same subject. The evidence supports a change for one group, not a general rule for every student. A short check with the course office can resolve any remaining question about my own attendance.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a closed campus café: The café sign says it closes every Sunday. Today is Sunday, and the door is locked. A friend guesses the business has permanently closed, but there is no such notice. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：校園咖啡店沒開門。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The café must be closed to visitors at the moment, because the door is locked and the sign lists Sunday as a closed day. It cannot by itself prove that the business has closed permanently. The owner might be away or might be doing work inside, but I do not know. My friend might have misunderstood the sign because it only gives weekly opening hours. The café must have published some regular schedule, since we can read it at the entrance. I should check the current information or ask on an open day before making a claim about its future. For today, I can choose another place to meet my classmate. A simple observation supports a limited conclusion, not every possible explanation.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Read the clues about a practice recording with no sound: Your practice recording plays silently. The app shows that microphone permission was denied during recording. You can hear other audio on the device, but you have not checked the recording settings yet. Write a paragraph using must, might and cannot or can't, including at least one past deduction with have + past participle. Explain the evidence and say what still needs checking.
tasks.zh: 單元50加練：口說練習錄音沒有聲音。先依英文題目看線索，用 must 說證據很強的結論、might 說可能，用 cannot／can't 排除與明確線索矛盾的說法；至少一句推測過去的 have＋過去分詞。別把猜測當事實，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The silent recording might be connected to the missing microphone permission. The app's message is an important clue, but I should check the settings before claiming it is the only possible cause. The device cannot be completely unable to play sound, because other audio is audible. The app must have recorded a denied permission status, since that message appears on the screen. It might not have received microphone input during my attempt. I should review the normal permission settings and make a short test recording. I should listen to that test before recording a long practice answer again. The clues narrow the possible problem, but they do not justify a claim that the whole device is broken or that a new device is necessary.
tasks.focus: 推測：must／might／can't be（現在）、must／might／can't have + 過去分詞（過去）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a nursing skills centre in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：護理技能中心。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our nursing skills centre, which is on the ground floor of the teaching building, is an important place in my school life. Ms Lin, who supervises our practice group, explains each activity before we begin. The main practice room, where we work with training equipment, has clear spaces for different tasks. My classmate Amy, whose notebook contains careful diagrams, often helps me review the written instructions after class. We practise only the tasks approved for the session and ask the teacher when we are unsure. The small discussion area, which is beside the entrance, is useful for feedback afterwards. I like this centre because it gives our group a place to connect explanations with supervised practice. A clear goal makes each visit more useful than simply spending more time in the room.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a campus library tour in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：校園圖書館導覽。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: I recently showed a new classmate around our campus library, which has several different kinds of study space. Mr Chen, who works at the information desk, explained how to book a discussion room. We visited the quiet reading area, where students usually work independently. My friend Jenny, whose course includes a large reading assignment, was particularly interested in the nursing collection. The catalogue computers, which stand near the main shelves, helped us find a textbook without searching every aisle. We also checked the current opening hours and the rules for borrowing equipment. The library was more useful after we understood how the services fitted together. I told Jenny that asking a librarian is a sensible first step when a search becomes confusing, rather than assuming the book is unavailable.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a community learning centre in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：社區學習中心。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Last weekend, I visited a community learning centre, which offers public activities in several small rooms. Ms Wu, who coordinates the events, welcomed our student group and explained the day's plan. The front desk, where visitors ask about current activities, had a clear noticeboard. I worked with Kevin, whose volunteer role was to organise general information sheets. We followed the coordinator's instructions and directed questions outside our role to the appropriate staff member. The meeting room, which was beside the entrance, hosted a discussion about local services. I noticed that practical details such as signs and a clear contact point helped people find their way. The visit gave me a concrete example of how different non-clinical roles can support a community event without pretending to provide individual professional advice.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce an English conversation club in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：英語口說社。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our English conversation club, which meets after classes, gives me a place to practise familiar language with new people. Lisa, who organises the weekly activities, usually begins with one simple question. The club room, where we move the chairs into small groups, feels different from an ordinary lecture room. My partner Ben, whose main goal is clearer pronunciation, likes activities with short repeated exchanges. I prefer questions about student life, so we try to include both interests. The imaginary hospital map, which we used last week, gave us a reason to ask for directions without discussing any real patient. I appreciate the chance to make an imperfect first attempt and try again. A friendly activity with a clear purpose helps me speak more than a list of isolated words does.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a hospital visitor information area in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：醫院訪客服務區。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: During an authorised orientation, our teacher showed us a hospital visitor information area, which was near the main entrance. A staff member, who was responsible for general directions, explained the limits of that role. The counter, where visitors asked about locations and public services, had maps in several formats. My classmate Anna, whose assignment focused on clear communication, noticed that the map and the wall signs used matching names. A large printed guide, which remained visible beside the counter, helped people check the route at their own pace. We did not record personal information or enter areas outside our tour. The visit showed me that a useful explanation starts with understanding the person's question. When a request needs another team, giving a clear route to that team is more helpful than guessing.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a university careers office in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：大學職涯辦公室。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The university careers office, which is beside the student centre, helps students explore future study and work. Ms Huang, who advises our nursing group, encourages us to separate personal experiences from official requirements. Her meeting room, where we discussed my questions about work overseas, had space for a small group. My classmate Daniel, whose plan is still changing, asked how to compare several possible routes. The official source list, which the adviser showed us, was a useful place to begin checking current requirements. We also talked about preparing questions for alumni speakers. I left with a short list of things to verify rather than a promise about a future job. That made the conversation practical because I could work on one clear next step and review the plan again later.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a dormitory study area in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：宿舍自習區。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our dormitory study area, which is separate from the bedrooms, is a useful place for evening coursework. The resident adviser, who explains the shared-space rules, asks everyone to keep phone calls outside. The large table, where I usually review English, has enough room for a book and a notebook. My neighbour Mei, whose room is shared with two other students, often uses the area when she needs quiet. The noticeboard, which is near the door, lists the current opening times and a contact for problems. We try not to leave belongings on empty seats for long periods. I like having another study option without requiring my roommates to follow my exact schedule. A shared room works best when its purpose is clear and residents can discuss practical difficulties respectfully.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a first-year student mentor in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：大一學生的學長姐。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My student mentor, Jason, who is one year ahead of me, has helped me understand ordinary campus routines. We usually meet at the student centre, where there is a quiet public seating area. His planner, which separates classes from optional activities, gave me an idea for organising my own week. Another new student, whose journey to campus is long, joins some of our meetings and asks useful questions about timing. Jason shares his experience, but he reminds us to check formal requirements with staff. The library guide, which he helped us find, explains the booking process more clearly than an old screenshot. I value the meetings because I can ask small practical questions before they become larger difficulties. The mentor's role supports school guidance without replacing official advice.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a small student project team in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：學生專題小組。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our project team, which is preparing a presentation about community services, includes four nursing students. Amy, who is good at organising discussions, helps us keep each meeting focused. The shared document, where we collect approved sources and our own draft text, gives everyone one place to work. Kevin, whose main responsibility is checking the presentation order, notices repeated information between sections. I am preparing the introduction and a simple example. Our teacher, who reviews the outline at an agreed stage, asks us to explain how each point answers the task. We use fictional situations instead of private patient details. I have learned that a group project needs more than dividing the slides equally. Members also need to connect their ideas, check the final version and make space for questions from one another.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a campus transport hub in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：校園交通轉運處。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: The transport area near our campus, which connects several bus services, is part of my daily routine. Mr Wang, who works at the public information counter, helps visitors find current route information. The covered waiting area, where I usually meet a classmate, protects our books during rain. My friend Tina, whose placement schedule sometimes starts early, checks the first service carefully before planning a journey. The electronic display, which shows current service updates, is useful when a bus is delayed. We still compare the destination with our planned route instead of following the nearest group of passengers. I used to think travelling only meant knowing the departure time. Now I also consider the correct stop, the final destination and an appropriate contact if a delay changes my arrival.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a writing support session in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：寫作協助時段。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our writing support session, which takes place in a small teaching room, focuses on one useful revision at a time. Ms Lee, who teaches the group, asks us to explain the meaning before discussing a sentence. The shared screen, where she displays an invented example, lets everyone follow the same point. My classmate Eric, whose main difficulty is organising a paragraph, brings a short outline instead of a completed essay. I usually bring two versions of one sentence so that I can compare the changes. The feedback sheet, which we complete after the session, asks for a practical next step. I like this approach because the goal is visible and manageable. The next practice task gives me a chance to use the advice independently rather than merely copy a correction.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a family member who supports your study in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：支持你讀書的家人。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: My aunt, who enjoys learning languages, is one of the people who support my nursing studies. Her home in Tainan, where our family sometimes meets, is a comfortable place for a weekend conversation. Her notebook, which contains short English messages from her own practice, reminds me that learning can begin with simple sentences. My cousin, whose work schedule changes each week, also understands why a study plan sometimes needs adjustment. They ask about one thing I learned instead of only asking for examination scores. Last month, I explained a short paragraph about school life to them. Their questions helped me notice an unclear sentence. I appreciate their interest because it gives me a reason to express an idea clearly. Their support does not remove the work, but it makes the process easier to discuss.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a school open day in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：學校開放日。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our school open day, which introduces visitors to campus life, includes several student activities. Ms Yang, who coordinates our group, explained the schedule before the guests arrived. The welcome table, where visitors collected general maps, was my first assigned location. My classmate Claire, whose role was to guide small groups between public areas, checked the route with us beforehand. The demonstration room, which visitors entered with the responsible teacher, showed approved teaching activities. We answered questions about our own student experience and referred formal admission questions to staff. I enjoyed explaining why I chose nursing, but I also learned to say when I did not know an answer. A clear role helped me contribute confidently without making promises about the course or giving information beyond my knowledge.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

tasks.prompt: Introduce a reading group and its resources in one paragraph. Include at least four non-defining relative clauses using who, which, whose and where. Use commas, connect the details to a clear main idea, and explain why the people or place matter to you.
tasks.zh: 單元53加練：讀書會與閱讀資源。至少四個加逗號的補充關係子句，分別練 who、which、whose、where；介紹人物或地方，最後說對自己的意義。不能在這種補充句用 that，至少120字。
tasks.sample: Our nursing reading group, which meets twice a month, helps us discuss course materials carefully. The teacher, who selects the first few texts, gives us a narrow question for each meeting. The library discussion room, where we compare our answers, is small enough for everyone to speak. My friend Peter, whose notes often include a list of unclear terms, reminds us not to pretend we understand every word. The source list, which we check before using an explanation, keeps the discussion connected to the original material. We take turns describing the main idea and pointing to supporting details. I have learned that a confident statement still needs evidence. When our interpretations differ, we return to the text and ask the teacher about the point we cannot resolve together.
tasks.focus: 非限定關係子句：加逗號的 who／which／whose／where 補充說明（不能用 that）

grammar.title: 橋接段落：用當課句型，把時間、原因和轉折接順
points: 先看題目標出的「這一課的文法」，用那一課的句型回答任務；每題的重點不同，不必把所有高階句型都塞進去。
時間順序用 At first、Then、After that；寫哪個時間點，就配合當課學到的時態。
原因和結果用 because、so、As a result；轉折用 However，連接詞要符合前後真正的關係。
it、this、they 要能看出指的是誰或哪件事；最後一句收回這段重點，讓讀者跟得上。

examples.en: At first, I felt nervous during clinical practice.
examples.zh: 一開始，實習時我很緊張。

examples.en: However, my teacher explained the task again.
examples.zh: 不過，老師又把任務解釋了一次。

examples.en: After that, I understood the steps.
examples.zh: 在那之後，我了解了步驟。

examples.en: As a result, I felt ready for the practice.
examples.zh: 因此，我覺得自己準備好練習了。

mistakes.bad: However, but I asked my teacher for help.
mistakes.good: However, I asked my teacher for help.
mistakes.why: however 已經表示轉折，不要在後面再加 but。
